GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Weimar Constitution belongs to which country?

references.file: Tapestry source record: Weimar Constitution adopted

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The constitution established Germany’s parliamentary republic in 1919.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which organization was founded in 1945?

references.file: Tapestry source record: United Nations founded

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The UN was founded at the close of the Second World War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which EU institution is directly elected by citizens?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Direct elections distinguish Parliament from the other institutions listed.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: National ministers meet in which EU institution?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The European Council instead brings together heads of state or government.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which institution normally proposes new EU legislation?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Commission has the principal right of legislative initiative.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which institution checks how EU funds are accounted for and spent?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Court of Auditors performs the EU’s external financial audit.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which institution determines the EU’s broad political priorities?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Heads of state or government meet in the European Council to set direction.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Who commissioned Sanmartino’s Veiled Christ?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which principal UN organ is seated in The Hague?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Court sits at the Peace Palace in The Hague.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In contentious cases, who can be parties before the International Court of Justice?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The ICJ resolves disputes between states, unlike courts that prosecute individuals.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which organization has the International Court of Justice as its principal judicial organ?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The ICJ is a UN organ; it is distinct from both European courts and the International Criminal Court.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A broad rise in the general price level is called what?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Inflation concerns prices generally, not merely the price of one product.

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A fixed amount of money buys fewer goods when prices rise.

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: GDP measures production within the territory, rather than the government’s outstanding debt.

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Real GDP separates changes in output from changes in prices.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: To avoid double counting, GDP chiefly counts which goods?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Intermediate inputs are embodied in final output; counting both in full would duplicate value.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: GDP divided by population gives which indicator?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Per-capita output is an average, not a statement that everyone earns the same income.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Iliad and Odyssey are traditionally attributed to whom?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Who is associated with the Theogony?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Hesiod’s Theogony recounts the origins and genealogies of the gods.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Lorenzetti’s Good and Bad Government cycle was painted for which type of setting?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which element distinguishes a Roman amphitheatre from a conventional semicircular theatre?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which element carries a dome above a square bay through curved triangular surfaces?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A figure’s weight resting mainly on one leg is called what?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Ambrogio Lorenzetti’s Presentation at the Temple depicts the presentation of whom?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Boullée’s Cenotaph for Newton was primarily what?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which facade type is non-load-bearing?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What does “pilotis” refer to in modernist architecture?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which movement foregrounded industrial serial form and the viewer’s bodily experience?

references.file: Tapestry source record: Minimalism: serial form and the viewer's body

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which approach treats a work’s geographical site as an essential part of it?

references.file: Tapestry source record: Land art and site specificity

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Action painting is particularly associated with which broader movement?

references.file: Tapestry source record: Action painting and colour-field painting

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Advertising and mass-produced consumer imagery are especially associated with which movement?

references.file: Tapestry source record: Pop Art, reproduction and consumer imagery

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Pop Art reworked imagery from commercial and popular culture.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which tendency openly reintroduced historical quotation into late twentieth-century architecture?

references.file: Tapestry source record: Postmodern architecture and historical quotation

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Externally expressed services and structural components are associated with which tendency?

references.file: Tapestry source record: High-tech architecture and expressed services

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Mantegna’s Camera degli Sposi was painted for which family?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Très Riches Heures was commissioned for which patron?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The distorted skull in Holbein’s The Ambassadors demonstrates what?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Caravaggio’s Supper at Emmaus in London was painted in which year?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Donatello’s Gattamelata commemorates which commander?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Michelozzo’s Palazzo Medici was originally built for whom?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Gozzoli’s Procession of the Magi decorates the chapel of which palace?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Piero’s civic fresco of the Resurrection is in which town?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Who directed construction of Sant’Andrea in Mantua after Alberti’s death?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Who is portrayed in Leonardo’s Lady with an Ermine?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What happened to Leonardo’s great Sforza equestrian monument?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Carpaccio’s Saint Ursula paintings were conceived as what?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Bosch’s Garden of Earthly Delights is arranged as what?

references.file: Tapestry source record: Garden of Earthly Delights

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A “sacra conversazione” typically presents the Virgin and saints in what kind of setting?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Who commissioned Raphael’s Triumph of Galatea at the Villa Farnesina?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Sistine Madonna was originally made for a church in which city?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Dürer’s Rhinoceros woodcut was based primarily on what?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The title Madonna of the Harpies refers to figures on which part of the painting?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Titian’s Bacchus and Ariadne was made for which patron?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which expected object is absent from Pontormo’s Capponi Chapel Deposition?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Dürer presented his Four Apostles panels to which city?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Correggio’s Assumption in Parma Cathedral uses the dome to suggest what?

references.file: Tapestry source record: Assumption, Parma Cathedral dome

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The illusionistic composition visually dissolves the architectural boundary overhead.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Giulio Romano’s Fall of the Giants occupies a room in which palace?

references.file: Tapestry source record: Fall of the Giants

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The elongated proportions of Madonna with the Long Neck are associated with which tendency?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Cellini’s celebrated gold Salt Cellar was made for which ruler?

references.file: Tapestry source record: Cellini Salt Cellar

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A Burial at Ornans gives monumental scale to which subject?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Millais’s Ophelia draws its subject from which play?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Courbet exhibited The Painter’s Studio in 1855 in which setting?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Bellelli Family is principally which kind of work?

references.file: Tapestry source record: The Bellelli Family

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Le Déjeuner sur l’herbe was shown in 1863 at which exhibition?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which painter’s 1863 Birth of Venus exemplifies academic mythology rather than Manet’s contemporary nude?

references.file: Tapestry source record: The Birth of Venus

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Monet’s Impression, Sunrise depicts the harbour of which city?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Monet’s Woman with a Parasol of 1875 belongs to which phase of his career?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Dance at Le Moulin de la Galette chiefly depicts what?

references.file: Tapestry source record: Dance at Le Moulin de la Galette

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Renoir painted a crowded scene of modern leisure with changing outdoor light.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Thinker was originally conceived for which larger project?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: How many painted versions of Isle of the Dead did Böcklin produce?

references.file: Tapestry source record: Isle of the Dead: versions

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which phase of Van Gogh’s career includes The Potato Eaters?

references.file: Tapestry source record: The Potato Eaters

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which label was applied retrospectively to diverse artists rather than one unified group?

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Crucifixion, Scuola Grande di San Rocco is associated with Tintoretto. Large narrative composition within Tintoretto's Venetian cycle.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Saint George and the Dragon
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Saint George and the Dragon is associated with Paolo Uccello. London version used as the reference example; other versions exist.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Martyrdom of Saint Philip
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Martyrdom of Saint Philip is associated with Jusepe de Ribera. Formerly interpreted as Saint Bartholomew; subject corrected.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Pilgrimage to Cythera
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Pilgrimage to Cythera is associated with Antoine Watteau. Louvre reception piece; distinguish the later Berlin version.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Charles I at the Hunt
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Charles I at the Hunt is associated with Anthony van Dyck. Royal authority presented through apparently informal dress and setting.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A Rake's Progress
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A Rake's Progress is associated with William Hogarth. Eight paintings; engravings published in 1735.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Robinson Crusoe
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Robinson Crusoe is associated with Daniel Defoe. First publication of the novel.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Ognissanti Madonna
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Ognissanti Madonna is associated with Giotto. Tempera and gold on panel; volumetric figures within a Gothic throne.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Garden of Love
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Garden of Love is associated with Peter Paul Rubens. Prado painting; courtly couples, putti and a garden setting.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Portrait of Charles VII
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Portrait of Charles VII is associated with Jean Fouquet. Royal portrait now at the Louvre; approximate dating.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: San Zaccaria Altarpiece
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: San Zaccaria Altarpiece is associated with Giovanni Bellini. Sacra conversazione set within a unified architectural space.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Joy of Life
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Joy of Life is associated with Henri Matisse. Also called Le Bonheur de vivre. Fauvist colour and an idealised figure landscape; the handwritten placement is not a precise creation date.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Melun Diptych
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Melun Diptych is associated with Jean Fouquet. Étienne Chevalier and Saint Stephen paired with the Virgin and Child.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Uffizi palace
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Uffizi palace is associated with Giorgio Vasari. Built as administrative offices for Cosimo I; completed after Vasari's death.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Apollo and the Continents
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Apollo and the Continents is associated with Giambattista Tiepolo. Grand staircase fresco in Neumann's Würzburg Residence.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Abduction of a Sabine Woman
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Abduction of a Sabine Woman is associated with Giambologna. Giambologna; spiralling three-figure marble group.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Faust, Part One
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Faust, Part One is associated with Johann Wolfgang von Goethe. Part One publication; Part Two published posthumously in 1832.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Equestrian statue of Gattamelata
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Equestrian statue of Gattamelata is associated with Donatello. Padua; bronze monument to the condottiere Erasmo da Narni.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Fall of the Giants
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Fall of the Giants is associated with Giulio Romano. Palazzo Te; painted architecture dissolves the room's boundaries.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Valpinçon Bather
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Valpinçon Bather is associated with Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres. Figure seen from behind; an important precursor to The Turkish Bath.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Sarah Siddons as the Tragic Muse
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Sarah Siddons as the Tragic Muse is associated with Joshua Reynolds. Portrait identifying the actor with Melpomene; Huntington version.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: De pictura
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: De pictura is associated with Leon Battista Alberti. Latin treatise on painting; Italian version followed in 1436.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Grande Odalisque
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Grande Odalisque is associated with Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres. Orientalist subject and deliberately elongated anatomy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Las Hilanderas
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Las Hilanderas is associated with Diego Velázquez. Myth of Arachne represented through a tapestry workshop.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Blind Leading the Blind
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Blind Leading the Blind is associated with Pieter Bruegel the Elder. Biblical parable rendered as a sequence of falling figures.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: On the Infinite, Universe and Worlds
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: On the Infinite, Universe and Worlds is associated with Giordano Bruno. Italian dialogue; publication in London.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Venus, Cupid, Folly and Time
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Venus, Cupid, Folly and Time is associated with Bronzino. Allegory with deliberately complex iconography.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Well of Moses
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Well of Moses is associated with Claus Sluter. Chartreuse de Champmol; completed with workshop participation.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Charles V at Mühlberg
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Charles V at Mühlberg is associated with Titian. Commemorates the emperor's victory of 1547.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Sower
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Sower is associated with Jean-François Millet. Boston painting as a reference example; later variants and prints also exist.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: David, bronze
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: David, bronze is associated with Donatello. Approximate, debated date; distinguish from Donatello's earlier marble David.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Romeo and Juliet
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Romeo and Juliet is associated with William Shakespeare. Approximate composition; first quarto printed 1597.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Royal Saltworks at Arc-et-Senans
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Royal Saltworks at Arc-et-Senans is associated with Claude-Nicolas Ledoux. Industrial architecture; distinguish the built saltworks from the ideal city of Chaux.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Disputation of the Holy Sacrament
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Disputation of the Holy Sacrament is associated with Raphael. Theology fresco opposite the School of Athens.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Hunters in the Snow
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Hunters in the Snow is associated with Pieter Bruegel the Elder. Winter panel from a cycle of the seasons.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Robbers
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Robbers is associated with Friedrich Schiller. Published 1781; first staged in 1782.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Immaculate Conception of Los Venerables
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Immaculate Conception of Los Venerables is associated with Bartolomé Esteban Murillo. Distinct from Murillo's many other versions of the subject.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: History of the Art of Antiquity
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: History of the Art of Antiquity is associated with Johann Joachim Winckelmann. Influential account of ancient art and stylistic development.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: David with the Head of Goliath
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: David with the Head of Goliath is associated with Caravaggio. Borghese version; dates debated. Other versions have different chronologies.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Landscape with Saint John on Patmos
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Landscape with Saint John on Patmos is associated with Nicolas Poussin. Classical ruins and ideal landscape frame the sacred subject.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Ancient of Days
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Ancient of Days is associated with William Blake. Design for Europe a Prophecy; later impressions also exist.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Two Treatises of Government
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Two Treatises of Government is associated with John Locke. Published in 1689 with a title-page date of 1690.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres is associated with Nicolaus Copernicus. Heliocentric astronomical treatise; published in Nuremberg.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Summa Theologiae
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Summa Theologiae is associated with Thomas Aquinas. Thomas Aquinas's unfinished theological synthesis.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Napoleon I on His Imperial Throne
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Napoleon I on His Imperial Throne is associated with Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres. Imperial portrait invoking sacred and historical models of power.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Canterbury Tales
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Canterbury Tales is associated with Geoffrey Chaucer. Unfinished collection framed by a pilgrimage.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Four Apostles
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Four Apostles is associated with Albrecht Dürer. Panels presented to the city of Nuremberg.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: First Dresden Court Theatre
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: First Dresden Court Theatre is associated with Gottfried Semper. Original theatre; destroyed in 1869, later rebuilt to a different design.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Sydney Opera House opens
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Sydney Opera House opens is associated with Jørn Utzon. Opened after a long construction process; Utzon left the project in 1966.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Peace of Amiens briefly ended hostilities between France and which power?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1802 peace temporarily ended the war between Britain and France; fighting resumed in 1803.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The League of Armed Neutrality promoted by Catherine II sought to protect what?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The league defended the maritime trading rights of neutral powers during the American Revolutionary War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Louis IX died near Tunis during which expedition?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Louis IX's 1270 expedition to Tunis is known as the Eighth Crusade.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The English East India Company originally operated under which legal instrument?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Elizabeth I granted the company a royal charter in 1600, authorising its trading monopoly.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Wat Tyler is associated with which English revolt?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Wat Tyler was a leader of the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, which challenged taxation and serfdom.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Rome destroyed Corinth in the same year as which other ancient city?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Both Corinth and Carthage were destroyed by Roman armies in 146 BCE.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which defeated power rejoined the European concert at Aix-la-Chapelle in 1818?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The congress ended the Allied occupation of France and admitted it to the concert of major European powers.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Greek War of Independence sought separation from which empire?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Greek independence from Ottoman rule was internationally recognised in 1830.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: European Union established
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: European Union established: 1993. The Maastricht Treaty entered into force on 1 November.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Foucault's pendulum provides a demonstration of what?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The changing orientation of the swing relative to the ground demonstrates Earth's rotation.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Napoleon met Alexander I on a raft at Tilsit. Alexander ruled which country?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1807 settlement followed Napoleon's victories; Alexander I represented Russia.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Union of Utrecht brought together provinces in which region?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1579 union linked the northern provinces during the revolt against Spanish rule.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The abbreviation VOC refers to which trading organisation?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: VOC abbreviates Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie, founded in the Netherlands in 1602.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The German Empire was proclaimed in 1871 in which palace?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: William I was proclaimed German emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles during the Franco-Prussian War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Thomas More's refusal to accept royal supremacy brought him into conflict with which monarch?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: More refused to recognise Henry VIII as supreme head of the English Church and was executed in 1535.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: On which island did Napoleon spend his final exile?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Napoleon was first exiled to Elba. After Waterloo, he was sent to Saint Helena, where he died in 1821.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The capture of John II at Poitiers occurred during which conflict?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The English victory at Poitiers in 1356 was a major episode in the Hundred Years' War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Treaty of Tordesillas
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Treaty of Tordesillas: 1494. Iberian division of overseas claims.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: At Cannae, Hannibal defeated an army belonging to which state?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Hannibal's Carthaginian army defeated Roman forces at Cannae during the Second Punic War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Relief of Orléans
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Relief of Orléans: 1429. Joan of Arc participates in the French victory.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Boston Tea Party belongs to the background of which revolution?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1773 protest against British tea policy intensified the dispute between Britain and its North American colonies.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Otto I's imperial coronation is associated with the development of which polity?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Otto I was crowned emperor in Rome in 962, a foundational date in the history of the Holy Roman Empire.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The conquest of Granada ended the rule of which dynasty in Iberia?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Nasrid emirate of Granada was the last Muslim-ruled state in Iberia; it fell in 1492.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Treaty of Breda of 1667 ended a war principally between which maritime rivals?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Breda settled the Second Anglo-Dutch War, a conflict driven partly by overseas trade and naval rivalry.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Belgium's 1830 revolution sought independence from which kingdom?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The southern provinces broke away from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands to form Belgium.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The arrival of the First Fleet at Sydney Cove established a British colony on which continent?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The First Fleet reached Sydney Cove in 1788, marking the beginning of the British colony of New South Wales.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Alaric's army, which sacked Rome in 410, belonged to which people?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Alaric led the Visigoths. The later sack of Rome in 455 was carried out by the Vandals.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Thermidorian Reaction
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Thermidorian Reaction: 1794. Fall of Robespierre.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: First Council of Constantinople
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: First Council of Constantinople: 381. Separate event from the edict of 380.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Treaty of Hubertusburg concluded the central European phase of which war?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1763 treaty restored peace between Prussia, Austria and Saxony at the end of the Seven Years' War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Royal Observatory at Greenwich was founded primarily to improve which practical activity?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Founded in 1675, the observatory supported astronomical work intended to improve navigation at sea.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Francis I was captured at Pavia during which series of conflicts?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1525 battle was fought during the Italian Wars between French and Habsburg forces.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Peace of Utrecht
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Peace of Utrecht: 1713. Major settlement of the Spanish Succession war.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which trio participated in the First Partition of Poland?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Russia, Prussia and Austria divided Polish territory in 1772.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The battles of Legnica and Mohi marked the advance of which forces into central Europe?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Mongol forces invaded Poland and Hungary in 1241 and won at Legnica and Mohi.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Mary I's marriage to Philip linked the English crown to which dynasty?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Philip, later Philip II of Spain, belonged to the Habsburg dynasty.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Mary, Queen of Scots, was executed during the reign of which English monarch?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Mary Stuart was executed in England in 1587, during Elizabeth I's reign.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Treaty of the Pyrenees settled a conflict between which two monarchies?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1659 treaty ended the Franco-Spanish War and confirmed French gains along the border.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Luddites are chiefly associated with resistance to which development?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Luddite protests targeted textile machinery and changes to labour conditions in early industrial Britain.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Christianisation of Kievan Rus' under Vladimir I drew primarily on which tradition?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Vladimir's adoption of Christianity connected Kievan Rus' to the religious and cultural world of Byzantium.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Henry IV's journey to Canossa belongs to which dispute?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The conflict concerned relations between imperial and papal authority, especially the appointment of bishops.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Treaty of Campo Formio followed Napoleon's campaign in which region?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1797 treaty with Austria followed Napoleon's successful Italian campaign.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Charles Martel's victory near Tours was fought against forces of which caliphate?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The battle of 732 checked an Umayyad expedition into Frankish territory.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Napoleon's victories at Jena and Auerstedt were won against which power?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The twin battles of October 1806 shattered the Prussian army.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: NATO founded
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: NATO founded: 1949. The North Atlantic Treaty was signed on 4 April; West Germany joined only in 1955.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Rome's victory at Pydna ended the power of which kingdom?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Roman victory of 168 BCE defeated King Perseus and ended the Antigonid monarchy in Macedonia.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Edict of Thessalonica is associated with imperial support for which religion?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The edict of 380 endorsed the Nicene form of Christianity within the Roman Empire.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Jacquerie was a fourteenth-century peasant uprising in which country?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Jacquerie broke out in northern France in 1358, amid the disruption of the Hundred Years' War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The early Visigothic kingdom in Aquitaine was centred on which city?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: After the settlement of 418, Toulouse became the centre of Visigothic power in southern Gaul; Toledo belongs to a later phase.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Luther's Ninety-five Theses: 1517. Conventional opening of the Protestant Reformation.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Galileo's 1633 trial centred on his support for which astronomical model?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Galileo defended the motion of Earth around the Sun, in conflict with the Church's restrictions on Copernican teaching.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Henry VIII marries Anne Boleyn
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Henry VIII marries Anne Boleyn: 1533. Marriage preceded the 1534 Act of Supremacy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Imperial coronation of Charlemagne
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Imperial coronation of Charlemagne: 800. 25 December; Pope Leo III.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Battle of Castillon
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Battle of Castillon: 1453. Conventional end of the Hundred Years' War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Pepin the Short becomes king
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Pepin the Short becomes king: 751. Beginning of Carolingian royal rule.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: On the Origin of Species published
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: On the Origin of Species published: 1859. Darwin explained evolution by natural selection; distinguish scientific theory from later political misuse.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Battle of Kosovo
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Battle of Kosovo: 1389. Medieval Serbian and Ottoman forces; losses on both sides.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Diet of Worms
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Diet of Worms: 1521. Luther before Charles V.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Battle of Nicopolis
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Battle of Nicopolis: 1396. Ottoman victory over a crusading coalition.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Ivan IV crowned tsar
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Ivan IV crowned tsar: 1547. Tsardom of Russia.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Papal return to Rome
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Papal return to Rome: 1377. Gregory XI leaves Avignon.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Traditional foundation of Rome
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Traditional foundation of Rome: 753 BCE. Roman tradition; archaeological settlement predates this date.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Gunpowder Plot
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Gunpowder Plot: 1605. Failed plot against James I and Parliament in England.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Battle of the Milvian Bridge: 312. Constantine defeats Maxentius.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Saladin becomes vizier in Egypt
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Saladin becomes vizier in Egypt: 1169. Ayyubid rule begins in 1171.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Treaty of Karlowitz
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Treaty of Karlowitz: 1699. Ottoman territorial losses in central Europe.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Gregorian calendar introduced
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Gregorian calendar introduced: 1582. Initial adoption varied between countries.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Act of Abjuration
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Act of Abjuration: 1581. Dutch provinces reject Philip II's rule.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Fall of Constantinople
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Fall of Constantinople: 1453. Mehmed II conquers the Byzantine capital.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: War of Jenkins' Ear begins
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: War of Jenkins' Ear begins: 1739. Britain and Spain.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Outrage of Anagni
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Outrage of Anagni: 1303. Boniface VIII and agents of Philip IV.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Battle of Bosworth
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Battle of Bosworth: 1485. Henry VII defeats Richard III; Tudor dynasty.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: French invasion of Italy
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: French invasion of Italy: 1494. Charles VIII; Medici expelled from Florence.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Napoleon crowned emperor
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Napoleon crowned emperor: 1804. First French Empire.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: German Democratic Republic established
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: German Democratic Republic established: 1949. The East German state was proclaimed in October in the Soviet occupation zone.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Newcomen atmospheric engine
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Newcomen atmospheric engine: 1712. First successful commercial engine conventionally dated 1712.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: US Constitution signed
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: US Constitution signed: 1787. Constitutional Convention.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Teutonic Order founded
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Teutonic Order founded: 1190. Hospital fraternity at Acre; military order from 1198.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Columbus reaches the Caribbean
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Columbus reaches the Caribbean: 1492. First transatlantic expedition reaches Caribbean islands.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Edict of Nantes
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Edict of Nantes: 1598. Religious settlement under Henry IV.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis: 1559. Ends the principal phase of the Italian Wars.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Cabral reaches Brazil
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Cabral reaches Brazil: 1500. Portuguese Atlantic expedition.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Hijra
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Hijra: 622. Muhammad's migration to Medina; Islamic calendar epoch.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Decian persecution
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Decian persecution: 250. Empire-wide sacrifice requirement under Decius.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Pugachev's Rebellion begins
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Pugachev's Rebellion begins: 1773. Major uprising in the Russian Empire, suppressed by 1775.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Navigation Act
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Navigation Act: 1651. Maritime trade restrictions.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: École Polytechnique founded
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: École Polytechnique founded: 1794. Originally École centrale des travaux publics.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Assassination of Julius Caesar
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Assassination of Julius Caesar: 44 BCE. 15 March.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Mayflower voyage
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Mayflower voyage: 1620. Pilgrims and Plymouth colony.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: French First Republic proclaimed
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: French First Republic proclaimed: 1792. Monarchy abolished in September.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: League of Cambrai
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: League of Cambrai: 1508. Alliance initially directed against Venice.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Battle of Austerlitz
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Battle of Austerlitz: 1805. French victory over Russia and Austria.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Joseph Bonaparte placed on the Spanish throne
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Joseph Bonaparte placed on the Spanish throne: 1808. Peninsular War context.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Byzantine recovery of Constantinople
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Byzantine recovery of Constantinople: 1261. Michael VIII Palaiologos.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Battle of Tertry
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Battle of Tertry: 687. Pepin of Herstal consolidates power.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire: 1806. Francis II abdicates the imperial title.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Battle of Waterloo
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Battle of Waterloo: 1815. 18 June; Napoleon's final defeat.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Magna Carta
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Magna Carta: 1215. King John and the barons.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Valois dynasty begins
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Valois dynasty begins: 1328. Philip VI succeeds the direct Capetian line.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle: 1748. Ends the Austrian Succession war.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Acts of Union
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Acts of Union: 1707. Kingdom of Great Britain formed.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Battle of Trafalgar
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Battle of Trafalgar: 1805. Nelson's naval victory.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Tennis Court Oath
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Tennis Court Oath: 1789. 20 June; French National Assembly.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Italian republic referendum
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Italian republic referendum: 1946. Voting on 2–3 June chose a republic; Enrico De Nicola became provisional head of state later that month.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Jamestown founded
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Jamestown founded: 1607. English settlement in Virginia.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Treaty of Paris
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Treaty of Paris: 1763. Britain, France and Spain.

references.file: Original study question: referenced cultural or historical source

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Council of Europe is a separate international organisation focused on human rights and related cooperation.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The European Court of Human Rights applies which treaty?

references.file: Original study question: referenced cultural or historical source

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Court operates under the Convention within the Council of Europe system.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which group lists only the six founding members of the EEC?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg

references.file: Original study question: referenced cultural or historical source

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The EEC began with France, West Germany, Italy and the three Benelux states.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which city hosts the European Central Bank?

references.file: Original study question: referenced cultural or historical source

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The ECB is headquartered in Frankfurt am Main.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which classical architectural element comprises architrave, frieze and cornice?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The entablature rests on the columns and comprises architrave, frieze and cornice.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What was a Roman basilica principally used for before its adoption by Christians?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Roman basilicas accommodated public business and legal proceedings.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What is a rib vault's principal distinguishing feature?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The ribs articulate the vault and support the webbing between them.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A church with a central nave and two side aisles is usually described as having which spatial organisation?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The longitudinal nave-and-aisle arrangement is characteristic of basilican planning.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In Renaissance architecture, a rusticated façade emphasises what?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: The joints and faces of masonry blocks

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Rustication gives masonry a strongly articulated, often rough or recessed-joint appearance.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which feature distinguishes a giant order?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Columns or pilasters spanning several storeys

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A giant or colossal order extends across more than one storey.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What was the original civic function of Siena's Palazzo Pubblico?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The palace housed Siena's republican government.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural movement proposed megastructures and deliberately provocative projects in 1960s Florence?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Groups such as Archizoom and Superstudio challenged conventional architecture and consumer society.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In buon fresco painting, pigments are applied to which surface?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: In buon fresco, pigment becomes bound into the plaster as it carbonates.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which ingredient traditionally acts as the binder in egg tempera?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Egg yolk binds the pigments in traditional egg-tempera painting.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What does the technique of spolvero use to transfer a drawing?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A perforated cartoon allows powdered pigment to mark the design on another surface.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which process uses acid to bite lines into a metal printing plate?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Etching exposes selected areas of metal through an acid-resistant ground.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which printing method traditionally relies on the repulsion of oil and water?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Lithography separates greasy image areas from water-retaining non-image areas.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which metal is an essential major component of bronze?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Bronze is principally a copper alloy, traditionally alloyed with tin.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What does a pentimento reveal in a painting?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A pentimento is evidence of a compositional change made while the work was being painted.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which subject is represented by a Pietà?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A Pietà shows the Virgin with the dead body of Christ.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which saint is commonly identified by a wheel in Western painting?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The wheel refers to Catherine's traditional martyrdom narrative.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which saint is identified by the eyes she carries in this painting?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Eyes identify Saint Lucy, associated with sight. They can appear on a dish or, as here, on a stalk.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which saint's usual attributes include a lion and a cardinal's hat?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The lion and cardinal's hat are common attributes of Saint Jerome in Western art.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which apostle is traditionally represented with keys?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The keys refer to Christ's charge to Peter in the Gospel of Matthew.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which artist's paintings of railway stations, empty squares and long shadows helped define Metaphysical painting?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: De Chirico's unsettling city scenes are central to Pittura metafisica.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Italian painter was associated with both Metaphysical painting and still lifes of bottles?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Morandi briefly explored Metaphysical painting before concentrating on still-life variations.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which intervention defines Lucio Fontana's Tagli?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Fontana's cuts make actual space part of the work.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which artist made the white works known as Achromes?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Manzoni's Achromes investigate surfaces stripped of conventional pictorial colour.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which artist is particularly associated with mirror paintings?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Pistoletto's reflective surfaces include the spectator and surrounding space.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which artist created maps embroidered by Afghan craftswomen?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Boetti's Mappa works combine geographical representation with collaborative embroidery.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Italian opera genre is associated with comic plots and everyday characters?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Opera buffa developed a comic tradition distinct from opera seria.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Puccini's Madama Butterfly is principally set in which Japanese city?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The story unfolds in Nagasaki, where Butterfly marries the American officer Pinkerton.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Italian theatrical tradition relies on stock characters such as Arlecchino and Pantalone?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Commedia dell'arte uses recognisable character types, masks and improvised performance.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which writer is associated with reforming Italian comedy through works such as La locandiera?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Goldoni moved comedy toward scripted dialogue and observed social character.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which novel follows the decline of a Sicilian aristocratic family during the Risorgimento?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Lampedusa's novel examines aristocratic change through the Prince of Salina.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which narrative device frames Zeno's Conscience?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Zeno writes autobiographical recollections in connection with psychoanalytic treatment.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which novel centres on Giovanni Drogo’s long wait at the remote Bastiani Fortress?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Buzzati's novel follows Giovanni Drogo's long wait at the remote Bastiani Fortress.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Italian poet developed the idea of the fanciullino, or little child, within the poet?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Pascoli describes poetic perception through an inner child capable of wonder.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which film movement favoured location shooting and attention to post-war everyday hardship?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Neorealism often used real locations and stories of ordinary people's social struggles.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which profession does the protagonist of Bicycle Thieves obtain before his bicycle is stolen?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Antonio needs the bicycle for his new job putting up advertising posters.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Visconti film centres on Sicilian fishermen and their economic exploitation?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: La terra trema follows a fishing family in Aci Trezza and draws on Verga.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Fellini film evokes a provincial childhood under Fascism?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Amarcord recreates a fictionalised provincial world drawing on Fellini's memories.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which film won the Palme d'Or and depicts Lombard peasant life in the nineteenth century?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Ermanno Olmi's film portrays rural life in Lombardy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Italian film director is particularly associated with the spaghetti western?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Leone's westerns helped define the Italian reinterpretation of the genre.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which peace recognised important communal rights of the Lombard League in 1183?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Peace of Constance regulated the relationship between the emperor and the Lombard communes.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which dynasty ruled Naples immediately before the Aragonese conquest of 1442?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Alfonso V of Aragon ended Angevin rule in Naples.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which agreement in 1454 sought to stabilise relations among the major Italian states?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Peace of Lodi helped establish a balance among the leading Italian powers.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Italian state was ruled by the House of Savoy before unification?

references.file: Original study question: cultural or historical reference

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Savoy monarchy's Kingdom of Sardinia became the institutional nucleus of unified Italy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The relief of Orléans belongs to which conflict?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The siege was lifted in 1429 during the Hundred Years' War, with Joan of Arc taking part.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which was the next ecumenical council after the First Council of Nicaea?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Nicaea met in 325; the First Council of Constantinople followed in 381.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which came first in Henry VIII's break with Rome?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The marriage took place in 1533, before the Act of Supremacy of 1534 and the later measures listed.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which battle conventionally marks the end of the Hundred Years' War?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The French victory at Castillon in 1453 is conventionally taken as the war's end.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which royal dynasty began with Pepin the Short's accession?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Pepin became king in 751, replacing the last Merovingian king.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Gunpowder Plot targeted which English institution?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The plotters planned to blow up the House of Lords during the opening of Parliament in 1605.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which power lost substantial central European territories under the Treaty of Karlowitz?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The settlement of 1699 followed Ottoman military defeats and transferred extensive territories to its opponents.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Act of Abjuration rejected the authority of which ruler?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Dutch provinces repudiated Philip II's sovereignty in 1581.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which pope was attacked at Anagni by opponents linked to Philip IV of France?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The attack on Boniface VIII in 1303 arose from his conflict with Philip IV.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The German Democratic Republic emerged from which occupation zone?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: East Germany was established in the Soviet occupation zone in 1949.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which document predates the French Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The US Constitution was signed in 1787; the French Declaration followed in 1789.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis ended the principal phase of which conflict?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1559 peace concluded the prolonged struggle for predominance in Italy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Decian persecution required inhabitants to perform which act?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Decius required sacrifices and certificates of compliance, placing Christians who refused at risk.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Napoleon placed Joseph Bonaparte on which throne?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Joseph became king of Spain in 1808, in the context of the Peninsular War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which dynasty restored Byzantine rule in Constantinople after Latin occupation?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Michael VIII Palaiologos recovered Constantinople in 1261.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Holy Roman Empire was dissolved during which wider period?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Francis II relinquished the imperial title in 1806 amid Napoleon's restructuring of central Europe.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which dynasty followed the direct Capetian line on the French throne?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Philip VI's accession in 1328 began Valois rule.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle of 1748 ended which war?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1748 settlement concluded the War of the Austrian Succession.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Acts of Union of 1707 united which two kingdoms?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The two kingdoms became the Kingdom of Great Britain.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Jamestown was founded in which English colony?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The English settlement of Jamestown was established in Virginia in 1607.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The German Confederation was established by which diplomatic settlement?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Congress of Vienna created the confederation in 1815.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Treaty of Ryswick ended which conflict?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The treaty of 1697 ended the Nine Years' War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which engagement is also known as the Battle of the Nations?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The multinational coalition defeated Napoleon at Leipzig in 1813.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Toscanelli's Atlantic proposal envisaged reaching Asia by sailing in which direction from Europe?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: His 1474 proposal envisaged a westward Atlantic route to Asia.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Ottoman foothold at Gallipoli chiefly facilitated expansion into which region?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Gallipoli provided a strategic foothold on the European side of the Dardanelles.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which state disappeared following the Third Partition of Poland?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The third partition in 1795 ended the Commonwealth's independent existence.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Charles I's Personal Rule was characterised by government without which body?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Charles I governed without summoning Parliament from 1629 to 1640.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Rosetta Stone's discovery preceded which achievement?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The stone was found in 1799; Champollion announced a major decipherment breakthrough in 1822.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Theoderic established Ostrogothic rule in Italy after defeating whom?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Theoderic defeated Odoacer and took control of Italy in 493.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Charles of Anjou's victory at Benevento ended the reign of whom?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Manfred was killed at Benevento in 1266, enabling Angevin rule in southern Italy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which king returned at the Restoration of the English monarchy?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Charles II returned in 1660 after the republican and Protectorate period.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Where was Napoleon first exiled after his abdication in 1814?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Elba was his first place of exile; Saint Helena followed his final defeat in 1815.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Brandenburg–Prussia personal union was associated with which dynasty?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Hohenzollerns united Brandenburg and the Duchy of Prussia under one ruler in 1618.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which dynasty came to power in Russia after the Time of Troubles?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Michael Romanov's election in 1613 inaugurated Romanov rule.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Jan Hus was executed during which council?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Hus was condemned and burned at Constance in 1415.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Treaty of Meerssen divided territories between which realms?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 870 treaty divided much of Lothair II's former kingdom between East and West Francia.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Who directed French government during Louis XIV's minority?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Mazarin was the leading minister during the regency and the young king's early reign.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which came immediately before the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Formation of the Confederation of the Rhine
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Confederation of the Rhine was formed shortly before Francis II relinquished the imperial title.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Kalmar Union linked Denmark and Norway with which kingdom?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The union of 1397 joined the three Scandinavian kingdoms under a common monarch.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Louis XIV began personal rule after whose death?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Mazarin died in 1661; Louis XIV then chose to govern without a chief minister.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which leader is associated with the establishment of Normandy?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Rollo's settlement with the West Frankish king in 911 underlies the conventional foundation of Normandy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: At Grunwald, Polish–Lithuanian forces defeated which order?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The battle of 1410 was a major defeat for the Teutonic Order.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Carlsbad Decrees sought chiefly to suppress which tendencies?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The decrees of 1819 imposed repressive measures against liberal and nationalist activity in the German states.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The House of Savoy acquired Sardinia in exchange for which island?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Savoy exchanged Sicily for Sardinia in 1720.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which state belonged to the Quadruple Alliance of 1815 but not the Holy Alliance?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Britain joined Austria, Prussia and Russia in the Quadruple Alliance; the Holy Alliance comprised the latter three.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Petition of Right was presented to which English king?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Parliament presented the petition to Charles I in 1628.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What is a hypostyle hall?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: A hall supported by many columns
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A hypostyle hall has a roof carried by rows of columns.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In a classical temple, the opisthodomos is at the:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The opisthodomos is the rear porch or compartment of a Greek temple.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Rustication principally concerns the treatment of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Rustication emphasises masonry blocks and their joints, often using rough or strongly articulated faces.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A narthex is usually found at the:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The narthex is an entrance vestibule or porch of a church.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A portico is supported primarily by:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A portico is a roofed entrance or walkway whose open side is carried on columns or piers.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which term describes a window divided into two lights by a central support?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A bifora has two openings, generally divided by a column or mullion.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What is an oculus?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: An oculus is a circular opening, such as that at the top of the Pantheon's dome.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In reinforced concrete, steel reinforcement primarily resists:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Concrete is strong in compression; reinforcement is placed especially where tensile stresses occur.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What does a curtain wall normally carry?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Its own weight and wind loads
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A curtain wall is a non-load-bearing exterior enclosure, transferring its own and environmental loads to the structure.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A cantilever is supported:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A cantilever projects from a fixed support, leaving its other end free.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A drawing produced by cutting a building with a vertical plane is a:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A section reveals the internal vertical organisation of a building.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In a Roman town, the main north–south axis is the:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The cardo is conventionally the north–south axis of a Roman town grid.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A Roman insula was commonly a:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: In Roman urban housing, insulae were apartment buildings accommodating multiple households.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which room in Roman baths was heated to the highest temperature?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The caldarium was the hot room, while the frigidarium was cold and the apodyterium was for changing.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The cavea of a Roman theatre contains the:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The cavea is the tiered seating area surrounding the performance space.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Roman pozzolana was valued primarily for making:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Volcanic pozzolana mixed with lime enables mortar to set through hydraulic reactions, including in wet conditions.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Temple of Athena Nike on the Acropolis belongs to which order?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The small amphiprostyle temple uses the Ionic order.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The temples of Hera and Athena at Paestum are in which Italian region?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Ancient Paestum lies near the Tyrrhenian coast in Campania.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Erechtheion is particularly associated with which sculptural supports?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Its south porch uses female figures known as caryatids in place of conventional columns.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Maison Carrée at Nîmes is a surviving:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Maison Carrée is a well-preserved Roman temple from the early imperial period.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Trajan's Markets in Rome are notably constructed using:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The complex exemplifies Roman brick-faced concrete construction and vaulted spaces.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Pont du Gard carried water to which Roman city?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The aqueduct supplied Nemausus, modern Nîmes.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Arch of Constantine incorporates reliefs from:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The arch reuses sculptural material associated with earlier emperors, a major example of spolia.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Charlemagne's Palatine Chapel at Aachen drew notably on the model of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The centrally planned church at Aachen was influenced by late-antique models including San Vitale.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A westwork is a monumental structure at a church's:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A westwork is a substantial western entrance block, often with towers and upper rooms.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The monastery of Cluny belonged to which order?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Cluny was a major centre of reformed Benedictine monasticism.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The abbey of Fontenay is located in:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Fontenay is a major surviving Cistercian abbey in Burgundy, France.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The baptistery of Parma is closely associated with:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Antelami is associated with its design and sculptural programme at the transition from Romanesque to Gothic.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Basilica of Saint Francis at Assisi consists notably of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The complex has an Upper Church and a Lower Church, built one above the other.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Sainte-Chapelle in Paris is a major example of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Its slender structure and extensive stained glass exemplify Rayonnant Gothic.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which feature is especially characteristic of English Perpendicular Gothic?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Perpendicular Gothic emphasises strong vertical lines and panel-like window tracery.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In Gothic architecture, tracery is the:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Tracery subdivides window openings into ornamental patterns supporting the glazing.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A gargoyle differs from a purely decorative grotesque because it:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A gargoyle is a carved waterspout, whereas a grotesque need not have a drainage function.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The dome of Florence Cathedral was constructed without:
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Full timber centring below the entire dome
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Brunelleschi's method avoided the full supporting timber centring normally used for such a span.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Brunelleschi's Ospedale degli Innocenti was designed as a:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Florentine institution cared for abandoned children.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Pazzi Chapel is attached to which Florentine complex?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The chapel stands in the first cloister of Santa Croce.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Sabbioneta's Renaissance planning is associated with which ruling family?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Vespasiano Gonzaga developed Sabbioneta as a planned Renaissance town.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Villa d'Este at Tivoli is especially celebrated for its:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Its Renaissance garden is organised around terraces, fountains and elaborate water effects.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Teatro Olimpico's permanent scenery represents:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Vincenzo Scamozzi's stage streets use forced perspective behind the monumental stage front.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Scala Regia in the Vatican is especially associated with:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Bernini manipulated the columns and spatial dimensions to heighten the staircase's apparent depth.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Filippo Juvarra's Basilica of Superga overlooks:

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Boullée's celebrated design for a cenotaph honoured:

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Scream by Edvard Munch is most closely associated with:

references.file: National Museum of Norway — The Scream

sourceMetadata95.title: National Museum of Norway — The Scream

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Distorted form and intense colour convey psychological anxiety rather than detached observation.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What does sfumato do to painted contours?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Softens transitions so that outlines are not sharply defined
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Sfumato creates gradual, smoky transitions between tones. It concerns the handling of edges and shading, not simply the use of a dark background.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which approach is characteristic of Cubism?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Fragmenting forms and combining different viewpoints

sourceMetadata95.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Cubism

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which source of imagery was especially important to Surrealist artists?

references.file: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Surrealism

sourceMetadata95.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Surrealism

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Surrealism explored mental associations beyond ordinary rational control. Dream-like combinations may therefore appear even when individual objects are painted realistically.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which concern is closely associated with Impressionist painting?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Changing effects of light in modern life and outdoor scenes

references.file: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Impressionism

sourceMetadata95.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Impressionism

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Impressionist painters frequently explored transient light and contemporary experience. Visible brushwork helps record perception rather than conceal the process of painting.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which combination most closely describes a common Baroque pictorial effect?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Dramatic light, movement and emotionally charged action
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Many Baroque painters sought immediacy through strong contrasts and active compositions. This is a broad tendency, not a rule that every Baroque painting must look identical.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In bronze casting, the form of the model is reproduced using a:

references.file: Victoria and Albert Museum — Bronze casting

sourceMetadata95.title: Victoria and Albert Museum — Bronze casting

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A mould receives molten metal; casting permits more than one version of a model.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What does iconography mainly study?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Subjects, attributes and symbols represented in images
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Iconography asks what an image represents and how it can be recognized. A key, halo or particular gesture can help identify a figure or subject.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Luther’s Ninety-Five Theses chiefly challenged the practice surrounding:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Luther disputed claims about indulgences and the remission of punishment for sin.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In the Atlantic slave trade, what was the Middle Passage?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: The forced sea journey of enslaved Africans to the Americas

references.file: Royal Museums Greenwich — The Middle Passage

sourceMetadata95.title: Royal Museums Greenwich — The Middle Passage

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The term refers to a coercive transatlantic journey endured by enslaved people, not voluntary labour migration. It formed part of a larger Atlantic trading system.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A central aim of the Congress of Vienna was the restoration of:

references.file: UK National Archives — Congress of Vienna

sourceMetadata95.title: UK National Archives — Congress of Vienna

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The settlement sought a stable European order after the Napoleonic Wars.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What historical process does the term Risorgimento usually describe?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: The movement towards Italian national unification
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Risorgimento includes political, military and cultural movements connected with the formation of a unified Italian state. It is distinct from the Renaissance.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which concept is central to Marx and Engels’ Communist Manifesto?

references.file: UNESCO — Manifesto of the Communist Party and Das Kapital

sourceMetadata95.title: UNESCO — Manifesto of the Communist Party and Das Kapital

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The manifesto interprets social and political history through conflicts between classes.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which event triggered the July Crisis of 1914?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo
GENERATED43_FACTS.group: Outbreak of the First World War

references.file: Imperial War Museums — How the World Went to War in 1914

sourceMetadata95.title: Imperial War Museums — How the World Went to War in 1914
