GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Treaty of Versailles of 1919 was principally a peace settlement with which country?

references.file: Imperial War Museums — The Peace Treaties That Ended the First World War

sourceMetadata95.title: Imperial War Museums — The Peace Treaties That Ended the First World War

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Versailles was the main Allied peace treaty with Germany after the First World War. Other defeated states were dealt with in separate treaties.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The League of Nations was founded on the principle of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Members were to act collectively against threats to peace.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which leader was central to the Bolshevik seizure of power in 1917?

references.file: Imperial War Museums — What Was the Russian Revolution?

sourceMetadata95.title: Imperial War Museums — What Was the Russian Revolution?

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Lenin led the Bolsheviks during the Russian Revolution. He should not be confused with Stalin, who consolidated power in the Soviet Union later.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which United Nations body has primary responsibility for international peace and security?

references.file: United Nations Security Council — What Is the Security Council?

sourceMetadata95.title: United Nations Security Council — What Is the Security Council?

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Different UN bodies have different mandates. The Security Council’s responsibility for peace and security is distinct from health, education or labour programmes.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which example best fits UNESCO’s concept of intangible cultural heritage?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: A traditional craft practice passed between generations

references.file: UNESCO — What is Intangible Cultural Heritage?

sourceMetadata95.title: UNESCO — What is Intangible Cultural Heritage?

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Intangible heritage concerns living practices, expressions, knowledge and skills. Its transmission is central; it is not limited to monuments or museum objects.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What is a referendum?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: A direct vote by the electorate on a specific question
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A referendum asks eligible voters to decide a stated issue directly. It differs from choosing representatives in a general election and from conducting an opinion poll.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which person most clearly meets the standard statistical idea of unemployment?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Someone without work who is available and actively seeking a job
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Unemployment is not simply the absence of a job. Standard measures distinguish unemployment from being outside the labour force.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A country has a trade deficit when, over the relevant period, what is true?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: The value of imports exceeds the value of exports

references.file: US Bureau of Economic Analysis — International trade

sourceMetadata95.title: US Bureau of Economic Analysis — International trade

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A trade deficit describes a balance between imports and exports. It is not the same measure as a government budget deficit or public debt.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What is the opportunity cost of choosing one option?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: The value of the best alternative that is given up

references.file: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis — Opportunity Cost

sourceMetadata95.title: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis — Opportunity Cost

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Scarcity means that choosing one use of time or resources can exclude another. Opportunity cost focuses on the next-best forgone alternative, not all alternatives added together.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What makes an income tax progressive?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: The share of income paid in tax rises as income rises

references.file: US Internal Revenue Service — Understanding Taxes: Progressive Taxes

sourceMetadata95.title: US Internal Revenue Service — Understanding Taxes: Progressive Taxes

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Progressivity concerns the tax burden relative to income. Merely paying a larger cash amount does not by itself establish a progressive structure.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Why is street lighting commonly used as an example of a public good?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: One person’s use need not reduce others’ use, and excluding passers-by is difficult
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The key ideas are non-rivalry and difficulty of exclusion. A good does not become a public good merely because a government happens to own it.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What long detour can ships often avoid by using the Suez Canal?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Sailing around the southern tip of Africa

references.file: Suez Canal Authority — About Suez Canal

sourceMetadata95.title: Suez Canal Authority — About Suez Canal

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Suez connects the Mediterranean with the Red Sea, shortening many routes between Europe and Asia. The comparable shortcut through Central America is the Panama Canal.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Bosphorus passes through which major city?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Istanbul occupies both sides of the Bosphorus, between its European and Asian shores. The strait is a geographic feature, not simply a political boundary line.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which mountain system forms much of Italy’s northern boundary region?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Alps connect and divide several central and southern European regions. The Apennines, by contrast, extend along much of the Italian peninsula.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: How does a river delta generally form?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Sediment accumulates where a river enters a larger body of water
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: As a river slows on entering a sea or lake, it can deposit sediment. Not every river mouth develops a large delta, because waves, tides and sediment supply also matter.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What does latitude measure?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Angular distance north or south of the Equator

references.file: NOAA National Ocean Service — Latitude and Longitude

sourceMetadata95.title: NOAA National Ocean Service — Latitude and Longitude

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Latitude describes north–south position using the Equator as reference. Longitude describes east–west position using a reference meridian.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Why does local solar time change as longitude changes?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Earth rotates, bringing different meridians towards the Sun in turn
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: East–west position is connected to the timing of the Sun’s apparent movement. Civil time zones are human arrangements and do not follow meridians perfectly.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which seasonal pattern is characteristic of a Mediterranean climate?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Generally dry summers and wetter, mild winters
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The term refers to a climatic pattern found beyond the Mediterranean region as well. It does not mean that every day in winter is wet or every summer day is rainless.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What does urbanization usually mean in population studies?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: An increasing proportion of people living in urban areas

references.file: United Nations Population Division — World Urbanization Prospects

sourceMetadata95.title: United Nations Population Division — World Urbanization Prospects

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Urbanization concerns the urban share of a population. It is not identical to the physical expansion of a single city or to overall population growth.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What is the central journey in Homer’s Odyssey?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Odysseus’s return home after the Trojan War

references.file: Perseus Digital Library, Tufts University — Homer, Odyssey

sourceMetadata95.title: Perseus Digital Library, Tufts University — Homer, Odyssey

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Odyssey follows a difficult homecoming, while the Iliad centres on an episode of the Trojan War itself. The two epics are related but not interchangeable.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Don Quixote’s adventures repeatedly expose the gap between what?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Romantic ideals of chivalry and ordinary reality

references.file: Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes — Don Quijote

sourceMetadata95.title: Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes — Don Quijote

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Cervantes’s hero interprets the world through books of chivalry, often misrecognizing what he encounters. This tension drives both the humour and the novel’s larger questions.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In Mary Shelley’s novel, who is Victor Frankenstein?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: The person who creates the living creature
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Frankenstein is the creator’s surname. Confusing creator and creature can obscure the novel’s questions about responsibility for what one brings into the world.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which concern is central to George Orwell’s Nineteen Eighty-Four?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Political control through surveillance and manipulation of truth
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Orwell’s dystopia links political domination to control over information, language and memory. It is not a neutral prediction of every feature of the actual year 1984.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which issue is central to Ibsen’s A Doll’s House?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Individual autonomy and the expectations of marriage

references.file: University of Oslo — Henrik Ibsen’s writings: A Doll’s House

sourceMetadata95.title: University of Oslo — Henrik Ibsen’s writings: A Doll’s House

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The play examines the roles assigned within marriage and the conflict between social expectations and personal independence. Its title is not an indication that it is a children’s puppet play.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which of these works is an opera?

references.file: English National Opera — The Magic Flute

sourceMetadata95.title: English National Opera — The Magic Flute

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Magic Flute is a staged dramatic work with singing. The other choices are instrumental works, even though their forms and instrumental forces differ.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What is a typical feature of a solo concerto?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: A featured solo instrument interacts with an orchestra
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The relationship between soloist and ensemble is central to the solo concerto. It is a musical form, not merely a synonym for any public concert.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which tendency is associated with Italian neorealist cinema?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Stories of ordinary people filmed with an emphasis on everyday social conditions

references.file: British Film Institute — A beginner’s guide to Italian neorealism

sourceMetadata95.title: British Film Institute — A beginner’s guide to Italian neorealism

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Neorealist films often engage postwar social life, locations and ordinary people. These are tendencies rather than an absolute rule about every actor or every shot.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What were intertitles used for in many silent films?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Displaying dialogue or information on text cards between shots
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Silent films could convey written dialogue and narrative information through intertitles. “Silent” therefore does not mean that audiences saw no language on screen.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Marie Curie’s research is especially associated with which phenomenon?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Curie’s work on radioactivity included investigations of radioactive elements. Recognizing her field matters more here than memorizing a list of biographical dates.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What did the World Wide Web add to the use of computer networks?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: A system for linking and accessing documents through hypertext

references.file: CERN — The birth of the Web

sourceMetadata95.title: CERN — The birth of the Web

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Web is a service built on network infrastructure, not another name for the entire Internet. Its linked documents made information sharing much easier.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Greenhouse gases warm Earth’s surface and lower atmosphere mainly by interacting with what?

references.file: NASA — What is the greenhouse effect?

sourceMetadata95.title: NASA — What is the greenhouse effect?

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The surface emits infrared radiation after absorbing energy. Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, affecting how energy leaves the climate system.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: How were many monumental tomb facades at Petra made?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: By carving the natural rock face

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Borobudur in Java is principally associated with which religious tradition?

sourceMetadata95.title: UNESCO — Borobudur Temple Compounds

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Angkor Wat belongs to the architectural heritage of which empire?

sourceMetadata95.title: UNESCO — Angkor

sourceMetadata95.verification_method: Author read the cited supporting web text; not independent expert certification.

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Angkor was a centre of Khmer power in Southeast Asia. Associating the monument with its civilization is more useful than memorizing the dates of individual restorations.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What was the central building of the Taj Mahal complex created to be?

sourceMetadata95.title: UNESCO — Taj Mahal
sourceMetadata95.support_summary: Shah Jahan built the white marble mausoleum in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.
sourceMetadata95.verification_method: Author read the cited supporting web text; not independent expert certification.

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Shah Jahan commissioned the monument in memory of Mumtaz Mahal. Although the complex contains other buildings, the famous central marble building is a tomb.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which civilization built Machu Picchu?

sourceMetadata95.title: UNESCO — Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu

sourceMetadata95.verification_method: Author read the cited supporting web text; not independent expert certification.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which combination describes Himeji Castle most accurately?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which material was central to Auguste Perret’s post-war rebuilding of Le Havre?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which setting most directly explains the historic street-and-canal pattern of Venice?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: A group of islands within a lagoon

sourceMetadata95.verification_method: Author read the cited supporting web text; not independent expert certification.

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Venice grew on small islands whose water channels became part of its circulation system. Its urban form reflects adaptation to the lagoon.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which project is an example of adaptive reuse?

GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Theatre — seating facing a stage; amphitheatre — seating around an arena

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What role does a cloister usually have in a monastery?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Covered circulation around an open courtyard

sourceMetadata95.title: Encyclopaedia reference — Cloister
sourceMetadata95.support_scope: Reference supplied for this topic; no claim that its live text was read in this pass.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A minaret is traditionally associated with which activity?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The perspectival vanishing point in Leonardo’s Last Supper is located near:

sourceMetadata95.title: Encyclopaedia reference — The Last Supper (Leonardo)
sourceMetadata95.support_scope: Reference supplied for this topic; no claim that its live text was read in this pass.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Piranesi’s Carceri are a series of:

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which pair of artists is closely associated with early Fauvism?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which contrast between mosaic and buon fresco is correct?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Mosaic — assembled tesserae; buon fresco — pigment applied to fresh plaster

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which subject would most naturally be classified as a still life?

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The cantilevered seat projects from its support rather than resting on rear legs.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which label is associated with Achille and Pier Giacomo Castiglioni's Arco lamp?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Flos produced Arco, which combines a heavy marble base with an arched metal stem.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Memphis group's furniture is especially associated with:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Memphis challenged functionalist restraint through deliberately expressive surfaces and forms.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which designer is associated with the phrase 'Super Normal', together with Naoto Fukasawa?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Morrison and Fukasawa used Super Normal to discuss understated, familiar everyday objects.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Lavoisier's explanation of combustion challenged the theory of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Lavoisier's work connected combustion with oxygen and undermined phlogiston theory.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which part of the atmosphere contains most of the ozone layer?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Stratospheric ozone absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which SI base unit measures luminous intensity?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The candela is the SI base unit of luminous intensity; lumen and lux measure related but different quantities.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which instrument is used primarily to observe objects too small for unaided vision?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A microscope magnifies small specimens; a telescope is designed for distant objects.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which of these forms of electromagnetic radiation has a wavelength longer than visible light?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Infrared wavelengths are longer than visible wavelengths; the other listed types have shorter wavelengths.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which dynasty supplied the monarchs of unified Italy?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Savoy monarchy expanded from the Kingdom of Sardinia to the unified Kingdom of Italy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Kingdom of the Two Sicilies was ruled immediately before unification by which dynasty?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The southern kingdom was ruled by the Bourbon dynasty until Garibaldi's campaign and annexation.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which agreement linked Napoleon III and Cavour before the war against Austria in 1859?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Plombières meeting established the basis for French support against Austria.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which conflict immediately preceded the transfer of Venetia to Italy in 1866?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Austro-Prussian War and Third Italian War of Independence
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Prussia's victory over Austria formed the wider setting for Italy's acquisition of Venetia.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which king of Sardinia abdicated after defeat at Novara in 1849?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Charles Albert abdicated in favour of his son Victor Emmanuel II after the defeat at Novara.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which political movement was founded by Giuseppe Mazzini to promote a united republican Italy?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Mazzini founded Young Italy as a republican nationalist movement in 1831.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Roman road originally connected Rome with Capua before extension toward Brindisi?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Appian Way became a major route from Rome to southern Italy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which ancient road linked Rimini and Piacenza?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Via Emilia crossed the plain south of the Po and gave its name to Emilia.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In the Roman Republic, which magistrates were chiefly responsible for state financial administration?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Quaestors held financial responsibilities, unlike the judicial role associated with praetors.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Twelve Tables are associated with the early codification of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Twelve Tables made a body of Roman law publicly accessible in written form.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which city was destroyed by Rome at the end of the Third Punic War?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Rome destroyed Carthage in 146 BCE after the final Punic War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Roman tradition of Cincinnatus chiefly exemplifies the surrender of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: In Roman tradition Cincinnatus relinquished the dictatorship after resolving the emergency, returning to private life.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Under the Roman Tetrarchy, how many rulers held the senior title Augustus at one time?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The tetrarchic scheme had two senior Augusti and two junior Caesars.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Justinian's general Belisarius reconquered North Africa from the:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Belisarius defeated the Vandal kingdom in North Africa during Justinian's reconquests.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which kingdom made Ravenna its capital under Theodoric?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Theodoric ruled Italy from Ravenna, where monuments preserve evidence of Ostrogothic patronage.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which people established a kingdom in Italy with Pavia as its capital?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Pavia became the capital of the Lombard kingdom in northern Italy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which scholar from York helped organise learning at Charlemagne's court?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Alcuin of York was a major figure in the educational reforms associated with the Carolingian Renaissance.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Golden Bull of 1356 regulated chiefly the selection of the:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Golden Bull formalised the role of seven prince-electors in electing the king who would become emperor.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The humiliation at Canossa involved Henry IV and which pope?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Henry IV sought release from excommunication from Gregory VII at Canossa.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which agreement conventionally ended the principal phase of the Investiture Controversy?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1122 concordat distinguished aspects of spiritual appointment and secular investiture.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Ciompi revolt in Florence involved chiefly workers in the:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Ciompi were workers in Florence's wool industry who sought political representation in 1378.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Pazzi conspiracy sought to overthrow the predominance of which family in Florence?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The conspiracy targeted Lorenzo and Giuliano de' Medici; Giuliano was killed, while Lorenzo survived.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The War of Chioggia was fought principally between which maritime rivals?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The late fourteenth-century war was a major confrontation between Venice and Genoa.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Italian League formed after the Peace of Lodi sought chiefly to preserve a:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The league was intended to sustain the balance among the leading Italian states.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which French king was taken prisoner at Pavia?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Francis I was captured by imperial forces at Pavia in 1525.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The imperial sack of Rome in 1527 took place during the pontificate of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Medici pope Clement VII was caught in the conflict between imperial power and its opponents.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Council of Trent began during the pontificate of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Paul III convened the council in 1545; it continued in several sessions under later popes.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Jesuit Matteo Ricci is particularly associated with missions and cultural exchange in:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Ricci worked in China and used knowledge of language, mathematics and cartography in cultural exchange.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: After the revocation of the Edict of Nantes, many Huguenots:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The revocation led many French Protestants to leave for other European states and overseas settlements.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Pragmatic Sanction issued by Charles VI sought to secure the succession of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Charles VI's Pragmatic Sanction aimed to preserve the Habsburg territories and permit female succession, benefiting Maria Theresa.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which city was the political centre of the Dutch Republic?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The States General met in The Hague; Amsterdam was a major commercial centre.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Ottoman capture of Constantinople occurred during the reign of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Mehmed II captured Constantinople in 1453 and made it an Ottoman imperial centre.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which commander led the Holy League fleet at Lepanto?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Don John of Austria commanded the allied fleet in the battle of 1571.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which monarch's break with Rome established royal supremacy over the English Church?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Henry VIII's religious settlement placed the English Church under royal authority.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Glorious Revolution brought William and Mary to the throne after the departure of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: James II fled during the revolution of 1688; William and Mary subsequently accepted the crown.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which work by Montesquieu analyses political institutions and the separation of powers?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Spirit of the Laws was Montesquieu's major comparative study of laws and political structures.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen was written by:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: De Gouges challenged women's exclusion from the rights proclaimed during the French Revolution.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The National Assembly emerged from representatives of which estate in 1789?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Third Estate deputies took the initiative in claiming to represent the nation.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The fall of Robespierre is commonly associated with:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Thermidorian reaction ended Robespierre's dominance and the central phase of the Terror.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Napoleon's coup establishing the Consulate is known as the coup of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The coup of 18 Brumaire overthrew the Directory in 1799.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Napoleonic institution centralised regional administration through appointed officials?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Prefects represented central government in the departments under Napoleon's administrative system.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which naval power remained Napoleon's major undefeated maritime opponent?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Britain maintained naval superiority and resisted Napoleon's Continental System.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Who became the first chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Adenauer was the first chancellor of West Germany, formed in 1949.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which statesman is associated with Franco-German reconciliation alongside Briand in the Locarno period?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Stresemann and Briand promoted reconciliation in the 1920s and shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 1926.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Dawes Plan addressed the problem of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Dawes Plan reorganised German reparations payments after the First World War and facilitated foreign lending.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Helvetic Republic was established in the territory of present-day:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Helvetic Republic replaced the old Swiss Confederacy under French influence in 1798.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Franco-Russian Alliance developed chiefly as a counterweight to:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The alliance linked France and Russia against the strategic influence of the central European powers.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Fashoda incident brought which two colonial powers into confrontation?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: British and French forces confronted one another at Fashoda in the Sudan in 1898.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which dynasty ruled Austria-Hungary until 1918?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Habsburg-Lorraine dynasty headed the dual monarchy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Nansen passport was devised chiefly to assist:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The internationally recognised identity document helped refugees and stateless people travel when they lacked a national passport.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which US president promoted the League of Nations in his postwar peace programme?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Wilson's Fourteen Points included an association of nations, though the United States did not join the League.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which territory became a source of conflict between Germany and France after 1871?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Germany annexed Alsace and part of Lorraine after the Franco-Prussian War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The term 'Roman Question' arose chiefly after which event?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: The capture of Rome by Italy
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The loss of papal temporal rule in Rome created the dispute later settled by the Lateran Pacts.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Albertine Statute was originally granted in which state?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Charles Albert granted the statute in the Kingdom of Sardinia; it later served as the constitution of unified Italy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which company founded by Enrico Mattei became central to Italy's postwar energy policy?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Mattei became the founding president of ENI, the state energy group created in 1953.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Taiping Rebellion was directed against which Chinese dynasty?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Taiping movement fought the Qing dynasty in nineteenth-century China.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact was concluded between:
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1939 non-aggression pact included secret arrangements concerning eastern Europe.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Soviet city endured a prolonged German siege during the Second World War?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The siege of Leningrad caused catastrophic civilian suffering from 1941 to 1944.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Atlantic Charter was issued by Roosevelt and:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Roosevelt and Churchill set out shared wartime aims in 1941.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which political development followed the Berlin blockade and airlift period in 1949?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Federal Republic and the German Democratic Republic were established in 1949.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which eastern European state did not join the Warsaw Pact?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Yugoslavia followed an independent socialist course after its break with Stalin and was outside the pact.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Hungarian uprising of 1956 was suppressed by forces of the:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Soviet intervention ended the uprising and restored a government aligned with Moscow.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Polish trade-union movement was led by Lech Wałęsa?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Solidarity developed from Polish labour activism and challenged communist rule.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Charter 77 originated in:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The declaration and civic initiative called for respect for human rights in Czechoslovakia.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which agreement created the European Coal and Steel Community?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The six founding states pooled coal and steel production under common institutions.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The second treaty signed at Rome in 1957 created:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Alongside the EEC treaty, the Euratom treaty established cooperation in nuclear energy.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Ventotene Manifesto was developed under which circumstances?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Spinelli and Rossi developed the federalist manifesto while confined on Ventotene under Fascist rule.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: At Manzikert, the Byzantine army was defeated by the:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Seljuks defeated the Byzantine emperor Romanos IV at Manzikert, a turning point in the loss of Byzantine control in Anatolia.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Toussaint Louverture is associated with the revolution in:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Louverture was a leading figure in the revolution in French Saint-Domingue, later independent Haiti.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which territory became Bangladesh after separation from Pakistan?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: East Pakistan became independent Bangladesh in 1971 after a liberation war.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Apartheid was a system of legally enforced racial segregation in:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Apartheid institutionalised racial classification and unequal rights in South Africa.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which leader became South Africa's first Black president after the democratic elections of 1994?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Mandela became president after the end of apartheid-era minority rule.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Cuban Missile Crisis concerned Soviet missiles placed near which power?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Missiles installed in Cuba precipitated a confrontation with the United States in 1962.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which Soviet leader negotiated with Kennedy during the Cuban Missile Crisis?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Khrushchev led the Soviet Union during the 1962 crisis.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which two states were parties to the British–Irish Agreement accompanying the Good Friday settlement?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1998 settlement included an agreement between the British and Irish governments.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Dayton Agreement principally ended the war in:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The 1995 agreement provided the settlement ending the Bosnian War.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which empire dissolved after the First World War, giving way to the Republic of Turkey in its core territory?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Turkish republic emerged after the Ottoman collapse and the Turkish War of Independence.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which city became the capital of the Turkish republic under Atatürk?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The republic established Ankara as its capital rather than retaining Istanbul.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Meiji reforms formally ended the rule of which institution?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The restoration displaced the Tokugawa shogunate and reorganised Japanese government around imperial authority.

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Guadalcanal is in the Solomon Islands, where the 1942–43 campaign became a major Pacific turning point.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Palazzo Carignano?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Villa Farnese at Caprarola?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Santo Spirito?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with San Sebastiano?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with La Scala?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Temple of Concordia?

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Arab World Institute?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Arab World Institute in Paris belongs to High-tech. Its defining role is cultural institute with patterned light-control devices.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Royal Palace of Caserta?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Royal Palace of Caserta in Caserta belongs to Baroque. Its defining role is bourbon royal residence.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Modena Cathedral?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Modena Cathedral in Modena belongs to Romanesque. Its defining role is cathedral.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Horta’s Hôtel Tassel integrates an open stair hall with daylight entering principally from:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The central stair hall is lit from above, helping unite the interior across levels.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Yale Art and Architecture Building?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Yale Art and Architecture Building in New Haven belongs to Brutalism. Its defining role is university building with textured concrete.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with San Miniato al Monte?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: San Miniato al Monte in Florence belongs to Romanesque. Its defining role is basilica.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Milan Cathedral?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Milan Cathedral in Milan belongs to Gothic. Its defining role is cathedral in candoglia marble.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Glyptothek?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Glyptothek in Munich belongs to Neoclassical. Its defining role is sculpture museum.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Terragni’s Casa del Fascio in Como organises its spaces around a:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Its compact block is organised around a central assembly space, linking circulation and public functions.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Vierzehnheiligen?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Vierzehnheiligen in Bad Staffelstein belongs to Baroque. Its defining role is pilgrimage church.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Schröder House?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Schröder House in Utrecht belongs to De Stijl. Its defining role is house with transformable upper-floor partitions.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: A tetrastyle temple front has how many columns?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Tetrastyle denotes a front with four columns; hexastyle has six and octastyle eight.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Vitra Fire Station?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Vitra Fire Station in Weil am Rhein belongs to Deconstructivist. Its defining role is fire station later used for exhibitions.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Nakagin Capsule Tower?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Nakagin Capsule Tower in Tokyo belongs to Metabolism. Its defining role is tower of prefabricated capsules.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Villa Farnesina?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Villa Farnesina in Rome belongs to Renaissance. Its defining role is suburban villa for agostino chigi.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with San Vitale?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: San Vitale in Ravenna belongs to Byzantine. Its defining role is central-plan church.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Il Redentore?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Il Redentore in Venice belongs to Renaissance. Its defining role is votive church.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Panthéon?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Panthéon in Paris belongs to Neoclassical. Its defining role is church converted into a national mausoleum.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with La Muralla Roja?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: La Muralla Roja in Calpe belongs to Postmodernism. Its defining role is housing complex of coloured interlocking stairs.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Guggenheim Museum Bilbao?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao in Bilbao belongs to Deconstructivist. Its defining role is art museum with titanium cladding.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with HSBC headquarters?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: HSBC headquarters in Hong Kong belongs to High-tech. Its defining role is bank headquarters with suspended floors.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with San Giorgio Maggiore?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: San Giorgio Maggiore in Venice belongs to Renaissance. Its defining role is monastic church with temple-front façade.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Rockefeller Center?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Rockefeller Center in New York belongs to Art Deco. Its defining role is commercial and cultural complex.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architectural tradition is most closely associated with Chartres Cathedral?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Chartres Cathedral in Chartres belongs to Gothic. Its defining role is cathedral with extensive stained glass.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What is a thermal bridge in a building envelope?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: A path of increased heat transfer
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: A thermal bridge conducts heat more readily than surrounding parts of the envelope, often at junctions or structural elements.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: At Hagia Sophia, what connects the main dome to the square arrangement of its four principal supports?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Curved triangular pendentives mediate between the circular dome and its supporting square.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The unusually shallow choir at Santa Maria presso San Satiro is resolved through:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Bramante created the impression of a deep choir within a very restricted physical depth.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Murazzi on the Venetian littoral were constructed primarily as:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The Murazzi are major masonry sea defences protecting parts of the Venetian lagoon's coastal barrier.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The church of Sant’Andrea in Mantua was built partly to accommodate pilgrims venerating a relic of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The church is associated with the relic of the Precious Blood, which helped shape its pilgrimage role.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which relationship is characteristic of the Laurentian Library vestibule's wall treatment?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: Columns appear recessed into the wall
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Michelangelo placed paired columns within wall recesses, challenging conventional classical articulation.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Teatro all'Antica at Sabbioneta was designed by:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Scamozzi designed the Teatro all'Antica as a purpose-built theatre for Sabbioneta's ducal court.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What visual effect characterises the Hall of the Giants at Palazzo Te?
GENERATED43_FACTS.value: The room dissolves into a painted catastrophe
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Giulio Romano's painted architecture and collapsing figures envelop the visitor in an illusionistic scene.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Sant’Ivo alla Sapienza was designed to serve which institutional setting?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The church stands within the historic Sapienza university complex in Rome.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which plan describes the main body of Bernini's Sant'Andrea al Quirinale?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The long axis of the oval runs across, rather than along, the entrance-to-altar axis.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The principal space enclosed by Bernini's colonnades in Saint Peter's Square is approximately:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The sweeping colonnades enclose an approximately oval space, connected to the basilica by a trapezoidal forecourt.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In an early Christian church, an ambo was used chiefly for:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The ambo is a raised platform for liturgical readings, distinct from the altar, font and episcopal chair.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Westminster Hall's medieval timber roof is a celebrated example of a:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Its hammer-beam construction spans the hall without a forest of supporting columns.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The central block and radiating wings at Stupinigi were designed around which court activity?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Juvarra organised a Savoy hunting lodge around a central ceremonial salon.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The engineering experience behind Paxton's Crystal Palace was particularly connected with:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Paxton transferred techniques of modular iron-and-glass greenhouse construction to an exhibition building.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which architect designed Habitat 67 in Montreal?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Safdie developed Habitat 67 as an arrangement of prefabricated concrete housing modules for Expo 67.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II combines shopping with which nineteenth-century spatial type?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Its glazed roof turns intersecting pedestrian routes into a sheltered commercial interior.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In Horta's Hôtel Tassel, ironwork and floor decoration are linked by:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The interior exemplifies Art Nouveau's integration of structure, ornament and spatial design.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The roofscape of Casa Milà is especially known for sculptural:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Gaudí treated rooftop services as an expressive architectural landscape.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The small metal discs visible on the Austrian Postal Savings Bank façade express the fixing of:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Wagner made the fastening of facing panels part of the façade's visual language.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: What does the glazed workshop wing at the Dessau Bauhaus chiefly reveal?

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The curtain wall wraps the structural frame, making the workshops appear unusually open.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The upper floor of the Schröder House can be reorganised through:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Its movable partitions allow the living space to shift between open and subdivided arrangements.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: Which feature occupies much of the upper level of Villa Savoye beside its enclosed rooms?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The roof garden is part of Le Corbusier's programme at Villa Savoye and one of his Five Points.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Barcelona Pavilion's walls chiefly demonstrate which idea?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Its freestanding wall planes articulate space without forming a conventional cellular load-bearing plan.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The broad horizontal roofs and low proportions of the Robie House are intended to emphasise:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Wright's Prairie architecture stresses horizontality and the extension of interior space into the site.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: In the Marseille Unité d'Habitation, internal streets principally provide access to:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The internal corridors serve apartments arranged within a large collective-housing structure.

GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: The plaza gives the tower an urban setting and a clear relationship to the street.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: At the Sendai Mediatheque, the irregular vertical tubes combine circulation and services with:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Toyo Ito’s tubes carry loads and accommodate services or movement through the open floor plates.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The shell segments of the Sydney Opera House were ultimately developed from the geometry of a:

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The widened upper portion of Torre Velasca is often read as a reference to:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: BBPR's modern tower evokes aspects of Milan's historic architectural skyline without copying it literally.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The bright service elements on the Centre Pompidou's exterior support which design strategy?
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Placing services and circulation externally helped create large adaptable interior spaces.

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The accessible ramps in the reconstructed Reichstag dome allow visitors to move above the:

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The thermal baths at Vals make extensive visual use of locally associated:

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Rolex Learning Center's continuous interior is characterised by:

GENERATED43_FACTS.subject: The Montreal Biosphere demonstrates the structural principle of a:
GENERATED43_FACTS.explanation74: Its spherical lattice distributes forces through a network of interconnected elements.

records.title: Linear perspective: horizon and vanishing point

records.title: Atmospheric perspective

records.title: Centralised plan and Renaissance ideals
records.note: Circular, square and Greek-cross plans can express geometrical order. A Greek cross has arms of approximately equal length, unlike a longitudinal Latin cross.

records.dateQualifier: Study period, not an event date

records.title: Disegno and colore

records.title: Fresco, tempera and oil: identifying technique
records.note: Buon fresco uses pigment on fresh plaster; tempera uses an emulsion binder; oil paint dries through oxidation. Support, binder and application are separate questions.
records.sourceMapping: Editorial study concept, not a photo transcription

records.title: Patronage, guilds and artistic commissions

records.title: Renaissance architectural proportion
records.note: Architects reinterpreted classical orders, symmetry and measured relationships. Classical appearance can coexist with new construction solutions and Christian functions.

records.title: Sfumato and chiaroscuro
records.note: Sfumato softens boundaries through subtle tonal transitions. Chiaroscuro models form through light and shade. The two terms are related but not interchangeable.

records.note: A Soviet-led coordination body for communist parties, distinct from the earlier Comintern.

records.title: Indian independence and Partition
records.note: British India became India and Pakistan amid mass displacement and violence.

records.title: Marshall Plan announced
records.note: A European recovery programme announced in June; implementation began in 1948.

records.title: Truman Doctrine
records.note: US aid to Greece and Turkey became a landmark in Cold War containment policy.

records.title: Brussels Treaty
records.note: Created the Western Union; the Western European Union followed the modified treaty in 1954.

records.title: Gandhi assassinated
records.note: Gandhi was killed in January after Indian independence and Partition.

records.title: Israel declares independence
records.note: The declaration on 14 May preceded an expanding Arab–Israeli war; consequences included mass Palestinian displacement.

records.title: Italian Constitution enters into force
records.note: Effective 1 January; the republican referendum was in 1946, not 1948.

records.title: OEEC established
records.note: Coordinated European recovery cooperation; the OECD succeeded it in 1961.

records.title: Republic of Korea and North Korea established
records.note: Two rival states emerged on the divided Korean peninsula.

records.title: Berlin Blockade and Airlift
records.note: Soviet blockade of western Berlin prompted an Allied airlift; the blockade ended in May 1949.

records.title: Federal Republic of Germany established
records.note: The Basic Law took effect in May; Adenauer became chancellor in September.

records.title: German Democratic Republic established
records.note: The East German state was proclaimed in October in the Soviet occupation zone.

records.title: NATO founded
records.note: The North Atlantic Treaty was signed on 4 April; West Germany joined only in 1955.

records.title: People's Republic of China proclaimed
records.note: Mao proclaimed the PRC on 1 October following communist victory on the mainland.

records.title: NATO, Warsaw Pact and non-alignment
records.note: The two military alliances structured much of Europe, but not every state belonged to either bloc. Non-alignment did not mean an absence of international interests.
records.sourceMapping: Editorial study concept, not a photo transcription
records.dateQualifier: Study period, not an event date

records.title: India becomes a republic
records.note: Its constitution came into effect on 26 January.

records.title: Schuman Declaration
records.note: Proposed pooling coal and steel production; a major step towards European integration.

records.title: Korean War
records.note: War began in June 1950; an armistice, not a peace treaty, ended major fighting in July 1953.

records.title: Notre-Dame du Haut, Ronchamp
records.note: Sculptural concrete forms distinguish this chapel from the geometric white villas of the 1920s.
records.setting67: Cultural / geographical association; see work context

records.title: Pop Art emerges
records.note: British and American strands use mass media and consumer imagery in different ways.
records.setting67: Cultural / geographical association; see work context

records.title: Brutalism, exposed materials and social programmes
records.note: Brutalism is associated with exposed construction and forceful form, often in public buildings. Not every concrete building is Brutalist, and the label has several origins.
records.sourceMapping: Editorial study concept, not a photo transcription
records.dateQualifier: Study period, not an event date

records.title: Pop Art, reproduction and consumer imagery
records.note: Commercial imagery, celebrity and repetition question distinctions between fine art and mass culture. Pop can be critical, ambiguous or fascinated rather than uniformly celebratory.
records.sourceMapping: Editorial study concept, not a photo transcription
records.dateQualifier: Study period, not an event date

records.title: European integration: ECSC, EEC and EU
records.note: Coal and steel cooperation preceded the EEC; Maastricht established the EU later. Signature and entry into force are different dates; the Council of Europe is a separate organisation.
records.sourceMapping: Editorial study concept, not a photo transcription
records.dateQualifier: Study period, not an event date

records.title: Treaty of Paris establishes ECSC
records.note: Signed in 1951 and effective in 1952; the Coal and Steel Community united six founding states.

records.title: Unité d'Habitation in Marseille completed
records.note: A postwar collective housing prototype combining apartments with shared services.
records.setting67: Cultural / geographical association; see work context

records.title: Stalin dies
records.note: His death opened a struggle for succession and later changes in Soviet policy.

records.title: Geneva agreements on Indochina
records.note: The settlement ended the First Indochina War and temporarily divided Vietnam.

records.title: Paris Agreements
records.note: Prepared West German sovereignty and NATO membership and established the Western European Union framework.

records.title: Warsaw Pact formed
records.note: Formed after West Germany joined NATO; the two alliances structured much of Cold War Europe.

records.title: Hungarian uprising
records.note: A revolt against Soviet-backed rule was suppressed by Soviet military intervention.

records.title: Khrushchev's Secret Speech
records.note: Denounced aspects of Stalin's rule; de-Stalinisation had uneven limits.

records.title: Suez Crisis
records.note: Britain, France and Israel attacked Egypt after canal nationalisation; international pressure forced withdrawal.

records.title: International Atomic Energy Agency established
records.note: An international body for cooperation and safeguards in the peaceful use of nuclear technology.

records.title: Treaties of Rome signed
records.note: Signed on 25 March; the EEC and Euratom treaties entered into force on 1 January 1958.

records.title: Cuban Revolution
records.note: Castro's movement overthrew Batista; Cold War alignment developed in the following years.

records.title: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum opens
records.note: The New York museum's spiral ramp organises a continuous exhibition route.
records.setting67: Cultural / geographical association; see work context

records.title: OPEC founded

records.title: Year of Africa
records.note: Seventeen African countries gained independence, within a longer and uneven decolonisation process.

records.title: Conceptual art
records.note: The idea, proposition or instruction can take priority over a unique crafted object.

records.title: Land art
records.note: Works engage sites and landscapes; not every work shares the same environmental ethics.

records.title: Minimalism
records.note: Industrial materials, repetition and the viewer's bodily relation to space challenge traditional composition.

records.title: Minimalism: serial form and the viewer's body
records.note: Repeated industrial forms and real spatial relationships shift attention from expressive brushwork to the viewer's encounter with objects.

records.title: Civil rights, feminism and social movements
records.note: Movements challenged legal and social inequalities through different goals and strategies. Compare voting rights, workplace rights and broader forms of social power.
records.sourceMapping: Editorial study concept, not a photo transcription
records.dateQualifier: Study period, not an event date

records.title: Conceptual art, instructions and documentation
records.note: The proposition or process may be central while objects, photographs or text document it. Conceptual art does not mean that material presentation is always irrelevant.
records.sourceMapping: Editorial study concept, not a photo transcription
records.dateQualifier: Study period, not an event date

records.title: Land art and site specificity
records.note: A work's location and physical conditions can be constitutive of it. Moving documentation into a museum is not equivalent to relocating the original site.
records.sourceMapping: Editorial study concept, not a photo transcription
records.dateQualifier: Study period, not an event date

records.title: Performance, body art and temporary work
records.note: An action, duration or bodily presence can form the work. Surviving photographs or videos may be documentation rather than the original event itself.
records.sourceMapping: Editorial study concept, not a photo transcription

records.title: Berlin Wall construction begins
records.note: East German authorities began closing the border on 13 August.

records.title: Gagarin's first human spaceflight
records.note: Vostok 1 orbited Earth on 12 April.

records.title: Campbell's Soup Cans
records.note: Serial presentation links consumer goods, repetition and art display.

records.title: Cuban Missile Crisis

records.title: European Communities Merger Treaty takes effect
records.note: A single Commission and Council served the Communities; the separate treaties did not simply disappear.

records.title: Arte Povera and unconventional materials
records.note: Artists used materials such as earth, cloth, wood and industrial components to question established artistic and economic values. Povera does not describe a lack of artistic skill.

records.title: Martin Luther King Jr. and Robert Kennedy assassinated
records.note: King was killed in April and Kennedy in June; distinguish their roles and circumstances.

records.title: Prague Spring and Warsaw Pact invasion
records.note: Czechoslovak reform efforts were suppressed by an invasion in August.

records.title: Apollo 11 Moon landing
records.note: Armstrong and Aldrin landed on the Moon; Collins remained in lunar orbit.

records.title: Postmodern architecture and historical quotation
records.note: Historical reference, symbolism and critiques of modernist uniformity take multiple forms. Postmodern is not a label for every building constructed after 1970.

records.title: High-tech architecture and expressed services
records.note: Structure and building services may be made visually prominent. Exposed ducts alone are insufficient to identify the movement or architect.

records.title: Khmer Rouge rule in Cambodia
records.note: Pol Pot's regime perpetrated mass killings, forced labour and widespread persecution.

records.title: Year of three popes
records.note: Paul VI died, John Paul I had a brief papacy, and John Paul II was elected.

records.title: Iranian Revolution and Islamic Republic
records.note: The monarchy fell and an Islamic Republic was established; the revolution brought together competing forces.

records.title: Transavanguardia named
records.note: An Italian critical label associated with a return to expressive painting.
records.setting67: Cultural / geographical association; see work context

records.title: Deconstructivist architectural form
records.note: Fragmentation and disrupted geometries challenge expectations of stable composition. The 1988 MoMA exhibition grouped diverse architects, not a single construction system.

records.title: Chernobyl nuclear disaster
records.note: A reactor accident on 26 April had widespread environmental and political consequences.

records.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
records.note: Border crossings opened on 9 November; German reunification followed in 1990.

records.title: Malta Summit
records.note: Bush and Gorbachev met during the rapid transformation of Cold War Europe.

records.title: Tiananmen Square crackdown
records.note: Chinese authorities violently suppressed a protest movement in June.

records.title: Globalisation and economic interdependence
records.note: Cross-border trade, finance, production and information increased interdependence. These processes predate 1989 and do not erase national institutions or inequalities.

records.title: German reunification
records.note: The German Democratic Republic joined the Federal Republic on 3 October.

records.title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
records.note: The USSR ceased to exist in December; successor states followed different political paths.

records.title: Maastricht Treaty signed
records.note: Signed on 7 February; the European Union formally began when the treaty entered into force in 1993.

records.title: European Union established
records.note: The Maastricht Treaty entered into force on 1 November.

records.title: NAFTA enters into force
records.note: A trade agreement between Canada, Mexico and the United States; later replaced by USMCA.

records.title: September 11 attacks
records.note: Al-Qaeda attacks in the United States reshaped international security policy.

records.title: Lehman Brothers bankruptcy
records.note: The September collapse intensified the global financial crisis; the crisis had begun earlier.

records.title: Arab Spring uprisings begin
records.note: Beginning in Tunisia in late 2010, protests spread in 2011 with different outcomes by country.

records.title: Angkor
records.note: Angkor combines temples, reservoirs and urban infrastructure. Angkor Wat and the Bayon belong to different building campaigns; the long range describes the city, not one temple.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Taj Mahal
records.note: Shah Jahan commissioned this mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal. Read the white marble tomb together with its garden and symmetrical complex; it is a funerary monument, not a royal residence.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Borobudur
records.note: A Buddhist monument with square terraces below circular platforms and a crowning stupa. The ascending route organizes reliefs and repeated stupas into a spatial sequence.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Petra
records.note: Nabataean Petra combined caravan commerce, rock-cut architecture and careful water management. Carved facades do not mean that every part of the city was cut into rock.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Machu Picchu
records.note: The Inca site joins stone buildings, terraces and steep mountain terrain. Its fifteenth-century setting distinguishes it from earlier Andean cultures such as the Moche.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Chichén Itzá
records.note: Temple pyramids, a large ball court and other monuments show a Maya city with wider Mesoamerican connections. Do not confuse it with Teotihuacan in central Mexico.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Teotihuacan
records.note: The Avenue of the Dead links monumental precincts including the Sun and Moon pyramids. The city flourished many centuries before the Aztec Empire; its builders should not be labelled Aztec.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Rapa Nui: moai
records.note: The moai are monumental stone figures associated with a Polynesian island society. Many stand on ceremonial platforms called ahu. The range is a broad period, not a date for every statue.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Himeji Castle
records.note: White plastered surfaces cover a sophisticated timber castle. Gates, walls and routes form a defensive system: its appearance is not simply ornamental.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Forbidden City
records.note: Beijing's imperial palace developed as a hierarchy of courts and halls along an axis. The initial Ming construction dates do not imply that every surviving structure is original.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Temple of Heaven
records.note: This ceremonial complex relates imperial ritual to ideas of heaven and earth. Read its symbolism and layout as a religious-political landscape rather than a residential palace.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Potala Palace
records.note: The palace was a winter residence of the Dalai Lama and a centre of Tibetan Buddhist authority. Its major seventeenth-century development stands on a site with earlier history.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Lalibela: rock-hewn churches
records.note: Eleven medieval churches were carved from rock and connected by trenches and passages. Excavating spaces and leaving structural masses produces architecture by subtraction.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Great Zimbabwe
records.note: The ruins record a Shona urban and trading centre. Carefully fitted granite walls, especially the Great Enclosure, challenge the idea that monumental African architecture was limited to Egypt.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Djenné: historic town
records.note: Earthen construction links the town's buildings to local materials and continuing maintenance. The range describes a historic urban phase, not the construction date of today's Great Mosque.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Persepolis
records.note: Darius I began the Achaemenid palace complex on a monumental terrace. Reliefs and ceremonial spaces expressed imperial authority; this is not a Greek polis.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Sanchi
records.note: Stupas, gateways and other remains trace a long Buddhist history beginning in the Mauryan period. The stupa is a sacred mound or reliquary monument, not an ordinary dwelling.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Khajuraho
records.note: The surviving temples combine towered sanctuaries with extensive sculpture. Both Hindu and Jain monuments are represented; reducing the site to erotic imagery misses its wider religious programme.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Bagan
records.note: Thousands of Buddhist monuments form a landscape shaped by patronage and merit-making. The selected range describes the principal building era, not every restoration.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Samarkand
records.note: Samarkand links Silk Road exchange with Timurid monuments and scholarship. The Registan, Bibi-Khanum Mosque and Ulugh Beg's observatory have different functions and building histories.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Hampi
records.note: The former Vijayanagara capital brings together temples, royal structures and a dramatic rocky landscape. The ruins belong to a major southern Indian kingdom, not to Mughal Agra.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Konark Sun Temple
records.note: The temple gives architectural form to the chariot of Surya, the sun god. Carved wheels and horses turn an entire building into a religious image.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Mogao Caves
records.note: Wall paintings and sculpture preserve many centuries of Buddhist art along the Silk Road. The caves also connect art history with manuscripts and intercultural exchange.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Longmen Grottoes
records.note: Rock-cut Buddhist images reveal changing styles and patronage, especially under Northern Wei and Tang rule. Compare carved stone at Longmen with painted cave interiors at Mogao.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
records.note: Look for tiny Mount Fuji beneath the crest and the three boats. This is a Japanese woodblock print from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, not an oil painting; size and framing make the mountain seem vulnerable.
records.setting67: Selected cultural context; dates describe the recorded phase

records.title: Shiva as Lord of Dance (Nataraja)
records.note: The dancing Shiva combines movement with balance. A drum evokes creation and a flame destruction; the figure underfoot represents illusion. The copper-alloy sculpture belongs to a Hindu context, unlike a Buddha image.

records.title: Stirrup Spout Bottle with Portrait Head
records.note: The portrait head is also a ceramic vessel, with a stirrup-shaped spout joining its passages. The Moche context predates the Inca Empire by centuries; shared geography does not mean a single culture or period.

records.title: Stonehenge
records.note: Megalithic construction combines upright stones and lintels. Study the monument as a sequence of prehistoric phases rather than a building made at one moment.

records.title: Skara Brae
records.note: Stone-built houses preserve domestic space and fittings. Compare this settlement with ceremonial stone circles: prehistoric architecture also includes everyday dwellings.

records.title: Newgrange
records.note: A passage leads into a chamber within a mound. Its carved stones and relationship to the winter solstice connect burial architecture, imagery and the seasonal cycle.

records.title: Mycenae
records.note: Fortification walls, the Lion Gate and tholos tombs belong to Bronze Age Greece. They precede the Classical temples of fifth-century BCE Athens.

records.title: Delphi
records.note: The sanctuary of Apollo linked an oracle, treasuries, temples and athletic competition. Its hillside setting differs from a regular urban grid.

records.title: Olympia
records.note: A sanctuary of Zeus and the setting of the ancient Olympic Games. Religious monuments and athletic spaces belong to the same complex.

records.title: Ephesus
records.note: The Library of Celsus and theatre exemplify monumental urban life. Distinguish the Roman city remains from the earlier fame of the Temple of Artemis.

records.title: Carthage
records.note: A Phoenician foundation became Rome's great Mediterranean rival. The archaeological site also contains a later Roman city; its remains do not all belong to one culture.

records.title: Leptis Magna
records.note: Public buildings, streets and harbour remains reveal a major Roman city in North Africa. Compare provincial Roman urbanism with monuments in Rome itself.

records.title: Timgad
records.note: Trajan founded the colony in 100 CE. The orthogonal street network makes it useful for learning cardo, decumanus and Roman planning beyond Italy.

records.title: Ajanta Caves
records.note: Monastic spaces, worship halls, paintings and sculpture form a Buddhist cave complex. Distinguish this context from Ellora's multiple religious traditions.

records.title: Ellora Caves
records.note: Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments coexist at Ellora. The Kailasa temple demonstrates how subtractive carving can produce an apparently freestanding architectural mass.

records.title: Elephanta Caves
records.note: The principal cave centres on Shiva and monumental sculptural programmes. It should not be classified as a Buddhist monastery simply because it is rock-cut.

records.title: Fatehpur Sikri
records.note: Akbar's planned capital combines courtly and religious spaces. Compare it with the later Taj Mahal: both are Mughal, but one is a city and the other a mausoleum.

records.title: Humayun's Tomb
records.note: A monumental tomb set in a formal garden, important for the development of Mughal funerary architecture. Its function and setting provide context for the later Taj Mahal.

records.title: Qutb Minar
records.note: The tall minaret belongs to an early Islamic monumental complex in Delhi. Its long construction history predates the Mughal period.

records.title: Tōdai-ji
records.note: An eighth-century Buddhist foundation associated with the Great Buddha. Present buildings include later reconstructions, so foundation and surviving fabric have different dates.

records.title: Itsukushima Shrine
records.note: The shrine's relationship to tidal water and the sacred island is central to its design. The twelfth-century development should not be confused with the dates of later repairs.

records.title: Brasília: civic centre
records.note: Lúcio Costa's urban plan and Oscar Niemeyer's civic buildings make Brasília a key modernist capital. Urban layout and individual buildings are related but distinct design scales.
creators: Urban plan: Lúcio Costa; civic buildings: Oscar Niemeyer

records.title: Chandigarh Capitol Complex
records.note: Le Corbusier's governmental complex connects exposed concrete, monumental form and climate-conscious design. It belongs to a planned city developed after Indian independence.

records.title: Zollverein: Shaft XII
records.note: The coal-mining complex links industrial production with carefully ordered modern architecture. Later reuse makes it useful for comparing original function and heritage adaptation.

records.title: Le Havre: reconstructed centre
records.note: Auguste Perret led the postwar rebuilding of the city centre. A consistent structural vocabulary and urban plan show modern reconstruction at the scale of a whole district.

records.title: White City of Tel Aviv
records.note: Modernist buildings adapt European design ideas to local climatic conditions. The district illustrates the international circulation and local transformation of architectural principles.

records.title: Fallingwater
records.note: Frank Lloyd Wright's house joins cantilevered terraces with a waterfall and rocky site. Learn the relationship between structure, interior space and landscape rather than treating the house as an isolated object.
