coverage.status: Six continuation sheets visually read and merged with the previous ten-sheet catalogue. Identifiable events, creators and works retained; some generic titles and cropped annotations remain unresolved.
pending: Sheet 1: the isolated Bison label does not identify a cave or object. It is retained in the source image without inventing a date.
Sheets 11–16: some generic artwork titles do not identify a version; these have contextual-identification labels and are not presented as exact transcriptions.
Sheet 16: torn/cropped lower-edge labels and partially visible presidential names cannot all be read. Original source images remain available.
coverage.notes: Dates distinguish depicted events, creation, publication, treaty signature and entry into force. Source sheets are available for comparison. The catalogue is an editorial study resource, not a guarantee of all possible ARCHED topics. New architecture context items supplement the photographs. V69 concept cards use approximate study windows, not invented dates of origin. They are editorial preparation topics, not verified past-exam questions.

polities.title: Roman Kingdom
polities.note: Traditional chronology; not a securely documented founding year.

polities.title: Roman Republic
polities.note: Traditional beginning; imperial settlement in 27 BCE.

polities.title: Roman Empire
polities.note: This segment ends at the lasting division of imperial rule in 395, not the extinction of Roman government.

polities.title: Western Roman Empire
polities.note: 476 is the conventional endpoint; Julius Nepos retained a claim until 480.

polities.title: Odoacer in Italy
polities.note: Rule in Italy after the deposition of Romulus Augustulus.

polities.title: Ostrogothic Italy
polities.note: Theodoric's conquest to defeat in the Gothic War; resistance continued afterwards.

polities.title: Lombard Kingdom
polities.note: Northern kingdom conquered by Charlemagne; southern Lombard duchies continued.

polities.title: Papal States
polities.note: Conventional beginning at the Donation of Pepin; interrupted in the revolutionary and Napoleonic era.

polities.title: Republic of Venice
polities.note: 697 is a traditional foundation; state formation was gradual.

polities.title: Republic of Florence
polities.note: Conventional republican span; included Medici dominance and interruptions.

polities.title: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
polities.note: Napoleonic interruptions 1801–1814; annexed to Sardinia in 1860.

polities.title: Kingdom of Italy
polities.note: Proclaimed in 1861; the visible chart stops at 1900, before the kingdom ended.

polities.title: Merovingian Franks
polities.note: Clovis's accession is used as a conventional starting point; multiple Frankish kingdoms existed.

polities.title: Carolingian realm
polities.note: Dynastic accession in 751; imperial title from 800; division at Verdun in 843.

polities.title: West Francia
polities.note: Partition at Verdun to the Capetian accession; change of dynasty rather than sudden creation of a nation.

polities.title: French monarchy
polities.note: Capetian accession to abolition of monarchy; several dynasties and disputed regimes within this span.

polities.title: First French Republic
polities.note: Republic proclaimed in 1792; Empire proclaimed in 1804.

polities.title: First French Empire
polities.note: First reign; the Hundred Days of 1815 are a separate restoration.

polities.title: Bourbon Restoration
polities.note: Interrupted by the Hundred Days in 1815.

polities.title: July Monarchy
polities.note: Louis-Philippe's constitutional monarchy.

polities.title: Second Republic
polities.note: Republic established in the revolution of 1848.

polities.title: Second Empire
polities.note: Napoleon III; collapse during the Franco-Prussian War.

polities.title: Third Republic
polities.note: Continues beyond this chart's 1900 boundary.

polities.title: Visigothic Kingdom
polities.note: Initially based in Gaul; much of Iberia conquered in 711; Septimania survived to 721.

polities.title: Emirate of Córdoba
polities.note: Independent Umayyad emirate; caliphate proclaimed in 929.

polities.title: Caliphate of Córdoba
polities.note: Dissolution followed by taifa kingdoms.

polities.title: Crown of Castile
polities.note: Permanent union with León in 1230; administrative transformation under the Bourbons.

polities.title: Crown of Aragon
polities.note: Dynastic composite monarchy; institutions abolished under the Nueva Planta decrees.

polities.title: Nasrid Granada
polities.note: Conventional foundation in 1232; capitulation to the Catholic Monarchs in 1492.

polities.title: Kingdom of Portugal
polities.note: Royal title in 1139; recognition in 1143; Iberian Union 1580–1640.

polities.title: Kingdom of England
polities.note: Unification conventionally dated 927; interrupted by the Commonwealth in 1649–1660. The monarchy was interrupted by the Commonwealth and Protectorate; see the separate restored-kingdom span.

polities.title: Kingdom of Scotland
polities.note: 843 is a traditional origin; formation of Alba was gradual. Separate royal institutions were interrupted during the Interregnum; annexation to the Commonwealth was proclaimed in 1654.

polities.title: Kingdom of Great Britain
polities.note: Political union of England and Scotland.

polities.title: United Kingdom
polities.note: Union with Ireland in 1801; territorial and name changes in the twentieth century. Ongoing state, not a 2026 extinction date.

polities.title: East Francia
polities.note: Eastern kingdom from Verdun; 962 marks Otto I's imperial coronation, not a universally agreed foundation.

polities.title: Middle Francia
polities.note: Partitioned at Prüm after Lothair I's abdication.

polities.title: Holy Roman Empire
polities.note: Conventional start at Otto I's coronation; decentralized polity, dissolved in 1806.

polities.title: Kingdom of Prussia
polities.note: A kingdom within a wider changing German political landscape.

polities.title: Austrian Empire
polities.note: Established before the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire.

polities.title: Austria-Hungary
polities.note: Dual monarchy after the Ausgleich.

polities.title: German Empire
polities.note: Unification under Prussian leadership.

polities.title: Kievan Rus'
polities.note: Conventional span from Oleg's capture of Kiev to Mongol sack; fragmentation began earlier.

polities.title: Grand Duchy of Moscow
polities.note: Conventional origin; tsardom proclaimed in 1547.

polities.title: Tsardom of Russia
polities.note: Imperial title adopted under Peter I in 1721.

polities.title: Russian Empire
polities.note: Continues beyond the displayed nineteenth century.

polities.title: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
polities.note: Union of Lublin to the Third Partition.

polities.title: Eastern Roman Empire
polities.note: Chart branches at 395; historians also use 330 or other starting points. Constantinople captured in 1204.

polities.title: Empire of Nicaea
polities.note: One of several Byzantine successor states; recaptured Constantinople in 1261.

polities.title: Latin Empire
polities.note: Crusader state at Constantinople, concurrent with Byzantine successor states.

polities.title: Restored Byzantine Empire
polities.note: Constantinople recovered in 1261, conquered by the Ottomans in 1453.

polities.title: Ottoman Empire
polities.note: 1299 is a conventional origin; expansion was gradual. Sultanate abolished in 1922.

polities.title: Sumerian city-states
polities.note: Approximate cultural-political grouping, not one continuous unified state.

polities.title: Akkadian Empire
polities.note: Approximate Middle Chronology dates.

polities.title: Neo-Assyrian Empire
polities.note: Conventional imperial period; fall of the last royal center in 609 BCE.

polities.title: Neo-Babylonian Empire
polities.note: Conquered by Cyrus in 539 BCE.

polities.title: Achaemenid Persia
polities.note: Conventional empire span; conquered by Alexander.

polities.title: Seleucid Empire
polities.note: Conventional Seleucid era to Roman annexation of Syria; territories shrank over time.

polities.title: Parthian Empire
polities.note: Accession is sometimes dated 248 BCE; 247 BCE convention used here.

polities.title: Sasanian Empire
polities.note: Ardashir's victory to death of Yazdegerd III.

polities.title: Rashidun Caliphate
polities.note: Conventional period of the first four caliphs.

polities.title: Umayyad Caliphate
polities.note: Damascus-based caliphate; Umayyad rule continued separately in Iberia.

polities.title: Abbasid Caliphate
polities.note: Baghdad phase ended in 1258; ceremonial Cairo caliphs continued 1261–1517.

polities.title: Great Seljuk Empire
polities.note: Coexisted with Abbasid caliphs; not a simple replacement of the caliphate.

polities.title: United Mongol Empire
polities.note: 1260 marks the succession crisis and fragmentation, not the end of all Mongol states.

polities.title: Ilkhanate
polities.note: Mongol-ruled Iran and neighbouring territories.

polities.title: Timurid Empire
polities.note: Timur's accession to the fall of Herat; successor traditions continued.

polities.title: Safavid Iran
polities.note: Isfahan fell in 1722; formal dynastic endpoint 1736.

polities.title: Qajar Iran
polities.note: Conventional dynastic span; coronation of Agha Mohammad Khan in 1796.

polities.title: Egypt: Old Kingdom
polities.note: Approximate conventional boundaries; chronology varies.

polities.title: Egypt: Middle Kingdom
polities.note: Approximate boundaries; intermediary periods deliberately left as gaps.

polities.title: Egypt: New Kingdom
polities.note: Approximate dynastic boundaries.

polities.title: Ptolemaic Egypt
polities.note: Ptolemy's royal title to Roman conquest.

polities.title: Kingdom of Aksum
polities.note: Very approximate span; origins and decline are not single dated events.

polities.title: Fatimid Caliphate
polities.note: Founded in North Africa; conquered Egypt in 969.

polities.title: Ayyubid Egypt
polities.note: Egyptian phase only; Ayyubid branches in Syria continued later.

polities.title: Mamluk Sultanate
polities.note: Egypt and Syria; conquered by the Ottomans.

polities.title: Mali Empire
polities.note: Approximate political span; decline and dissolution gradual and debated.

polities.title: Songhai: imperial phase
polities.note: Sunni Ali's accession to Moroccan invasion; earlier Songhai states predate this phase.

polities.title: Maurya Empire
polities.note: Approximate conventional dates.

polities.title: Gupta Empire
polities.note: Approximate imperial phase; regional successor dynasties continued.

polities.title: Imperial Cholas
polities.note: Approximate beginning of the medieval imperial phase.

polities.title: Delhi Sultanate
polities.note: Five successive dynasties; Lodi defeat at Panipat in 1526.

polities.title: Vijayanagara Empire
polities.note: Capital sacked in 1565; later Aravidu rule continued until 1646.

polities.title: Early Mughal rule
polities.note: Babur to Humayun's defeat; interrupted by Sur rule.

polities.title: Sur Empire
polities.note: Afghan interregnum in northern India.

polities.title: Restored Mughals
polities.note: Humayun's return; last emperor deposed in 1857. Some institutional chronologies use 1858 for the final transition.

polities.title: British Raj
polities.note: Crown rule; earlier Company rule was a different political phase.

polities.title: Shang dynasty
polities.note: Approximate start and conventional Zhou conquest date.

polities.title: Zhou dynasty
polities.note: Western and Eastern Zhou; royal power fragmented long before the end.

polities.title: Qin dynasty
polities.note: Imperial unification in 221 BCE.

polities.title: Western Han
polities.note: Ends at Wang Mang's usurpation; no historical year zero.

polities.title: Xin dynasty
polities.note: Wang Mang's rule; followed by civil war.

polities.title: Eastern Han
polities.note: Restoration under Guangwu.

polities.title: Sui dynasty
polities.note: Dynastic foundation 581; reunification completed in 589.

polities.title: Tang dynasty
polities.note: Interrupted by Wu Zhou 690–705; dates show the broad dynastic span.

polities.title: Song dynasty
polities.note: Northern and Southern Song; other states ruled northern China after 1127.

polities.title: Yuan dynasty
polities.note: Dynastic title in 1271; conquest of Southern Song completed in 1279.

polities.title: Ming dynasty
polities.note: Beijing fell in 1644; Southern Ming claimants continued afterwards.

polities.title: Qing dynasty
polities.note: Name proclaimed in 1636; Beijing taken in 1644; abdication in 1912. Museum period labels often begin at 1644.

polities.title: Kamakura shogunate
polities.note: De facto establishment in 1185; shogunal title granted in 1192.

polities.title: Ashikaga shogunate
polities.note: Authority fragmented in the Sengoku era.

polities.title: Tokugawa shogunate
polities.note: Shogunal appointment to Meiji Restoration.

polities.title: Meiji era
polities.note: An imperial era, not the lifetime of the Japanese state.

polities.title: Classic Maya city-states
polities.note: Approximate cultural period, not a unified empire; Maya societies continued after 900.

polities.title: Aztec Triple Alliance
polities.note: Alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan; defeated in the Spanish conquest.

polities.title: Inca Empire
polities.note: Conventional imperial phase; Neo-Inca resistance continued until 1572.

polities.title: Viceroyalty of New Spain
polities.note: Colonial administration; geographical extent changed.

polities.title: United States
polities.note: Independence declared in 1776; recognized in 1783. Ongoing state; 2026 is not an extinction date.

polities.title: Empire of Brazil
polities.note: Independence to republican coup.

polities.title: Italian Republic
polities.note: The 1946 referendum replaced the monarchy. The republican Constitution entered into force in 1948; these are distinct milestones.

polities.title: Vichy regime / French State
polities.note: Vichy exercised authority under occupation and collaboration. Free France contested its legitimacy; this label does not describe unified control of all French territory.

polities.title: Free France and liberation authorities
polities.note: The Free French movement and subsequent liberation bodies opposed Vichy and Axis occupation. Their coexistence should not be read as two tidy national borders.

polities.title: Provisional Government of the French Republic
polities.note: The provisional government restored republican legality after liberation. The 1946 Constitution opened the Fourth Republic; transitional institutions continued into 1947.

polities.title: Fourth French Republic
polities.note: A parliamentary republic under the Constitution of 27 October 1946. Its replacement in 1958 marks a constitutional change, not the creation of a new territory.

polities.title: Fifth French Republic
polities.note: The Constitution of 1958 established the Fifth Republic. The regime is distinct from the changing presidents elected within it.

polities.title: Weimar Republic
polities.note: The monarchy fell in 1918; the Weimar Constitution followed in 1919. The name distinguishes the parliamentary era from both imperial and Nazi Germany.

polities.title: Germany under Nazi dictatorship
polities.note: The Nazi dictatorship dismantled parliamentary democracy. Its territorial expansion and occupation policies cannot be represented by a fixed Central European border.

polities.title: Allied-occupied Germany
polities.note: Germany was administered in occupation zones after defeat in 1945. Two German states were established in 1949.

polities.title: Federal Republic of Germany
polities.note: Founded in 1949; German unity in 1990 extended the Federal Republic. Before 1990, the German Democratic Republic existed alongside it.

polities.title: German Democratic Republic
polities.note: The East German state existed alongside the Federal Republic until reunification in 1990. Shared dates here indicate coexistence, not equal territory.

polities.title: Commonwealth of England
polities.note: The monarchy and House of Lords were abolished in 1649. Parliamentary republican rule preceded the Protectorate.

polities.title: Protectorate of England, Scotland and Ireland
polities.note: Oliver Cromwell and then Richard Cromwell served as Lord Protector. The Protectorate was part of the wider Interregnum, not a royal dynasty.

polities.title: Restored Commonwealth
polities.note: The Commonwealth was briefly restored after the Protectorate. The monarchy returned under Charles II in 1660.

polities.title: Restored Kingdom of England
polities.note: The Restoration ended the Interregnum. England and Scotland remained distinct kingdoms until the Acts of Union of 1707.

polities.title: Restored Kingdom of Scotland
polities.note: Scotland's separate institutions were restored in 1660. The political union with England followed in 1707.

polities.title: Kingdom of the Netherlands
polities.note: The kingdom established in 1815 initially included the southern provinces. Belgian secession in 1830 and recognition in 1839 changed its territorial extent.

polities.title: Kingdom of Belgium
polities.note: Belgium separated from the Netherlands in 1830. Recognition by the Netherlands in 1839 is a later milestone.

polities.title: Russian Provisional Government
polities.note: Between the fall of the monarchy and the Bolshevik seizure of power in 1917. With year-level dating, several competing authorities appear in the same year.

polities.title: Soviet Russia: early revolutionary period
polities.note: Bolshevik rule emerged during revolution and civil war. The Russian Soviet republic was not yet identical to the later multinational Soviet Union.

polities.title: Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
polities.note: A union of Soviet republics, not simply a renamed Russian Empire. The union dissolved in 1991.

polities.title: Russian Federation: post-Soviet period
polities.note: This span marks the post-Soviet period. Other former Soviet republics became independent states; this regional column does not imply that they are part of Russia.

polities.title: Batavian Republic
polities.note: A republic established under French influence, followed by the Kingdom of Holland. The Dutch Republic before 1795 had a different political structure.

polities.title: Kingdom of Holland
polities.note: Louis Napoleon ruled the kingdom before its incorporation into the French Empire in 1810.

polities.title: Netherlands within the French Empire
polities.note: This is a period of annexation, not an independent Dutch kingdom.

polities.title: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands
polities.note: Independence was restored under a sovereign prince before the kingdom was proclaimed in 1815.

polities.title: Republic of Turkey / Türkiye
polities.note: The republic was proclaimed in 1923 following the end of the Ottoman sultanate. It represents one state in this broader regional column.

polities.title: Republic of China: mainland period
polities.note: The republic followed the Qing dynasty, but central control was fragmented. The 1949 boundary marks the government’s move to Taiwan, not the disappearance of the Republic of China.

polities.title: People’s Republic of China
polities.note: The PRC was proclaimed in 1949 on the mainland. This political chronology does not resolve territorial claims.

polities.title: Republic of China government on Taiwan
polities.note: The Republic of China government relocated to Taiwan in 1949. It is shown alongside the PRC to avoid erasing the distinct political chronology.

transitions.label: End of Latin rule in Constantinople
Conquest of Constantinople; Ottoman state predates it
Saladin ends Fatimid rule in Egypt
Qing entry into Beijing; not conquest of all Ming territories

worldCoverage.note: Selected political and cultural histories to 1900. Regional columns are reading guides, not fixed borders. Blank areas indicate gaps in this selection, not an absence of societies. Survival lines show political or cultural duration, never territory or power.

chapters66.title: Before states
chapters66.note: Settlement, ritual and the first visual cultures precede the territorial states below.

centres.title: Europe and the Mediterranean
centres.note: Material evidence, not a single state

chapters66.title: Cities and kingdoms
chapters66.note: Egyptian and Near Eastern state formation provides the wider setting for Aegean cultures.

chapters66.title: The Greek world
chapters66.note: Independent Greek cities coexist and compete; Persia and then Macedon reshape the balance.

chapters66.title: Hellenistic kingdoms → Rome
chapters66.note: Alexander's empire fragments; Rome expands through Mediterranean wars.

centres.title: Successor courts
centres.note: Greek culture across a wider world

chapters66.title: The Roman Mediterranean
chapters66.note: Imperial government and roads connect a large Mediterranean world; Christianity develops within it.

chapters66.title: A divided Roman inheritance
chapters66.note: Western imperial rule ends while the eastern court continues; kingdoms transform the western landscape.

chapters66.title: Caliphates and the Franks
chapters66.note: Islamic expansion transforms the Mediterranean; Frankish rulers consolidate power in the west.

chapters66.title: From empire to kingdoms
chapters66.note: Charlemagne's imperial project is followed by partitions; western and eastern kingdoms develop.

chapters66.title: Kings, emperors and the Church
chapters66.note: Papacy, empire and monarchies compete; crusades and expanding towns connect societies.

chapters66.title: Cities, courts and trade
chapters66.note: Mediterranean networks and urban patronage grow alongside kingdoms and religious institutions.

chapters66.title: Crisis and renewal
chapters66.note: Plague, war and church disputes reshape society; Italian urban cultures remain major artistic centres.

chapters66.title: Italian Renaissance centres
chapters66.note: Florence, Rome and Venice develop different forms of patronage; western monarchies consolidate.

chapters66.title: Italy in a wider struggle
chapters66.note: French and Spanish intervention in Italy overlaps with major Renaissance commissions and Atlantic expansion.

chapters66.title: Reformation and rival empires
chapters66.note: Religious division and Catholic reform intersect with Habsburg, French and Ottoman competition.

chapters66.title: Baroque Europe at war
chapters66.note: Rome is a major centre of Baroque patronage while the Thirty Years' War transforms European politics.

chapters66.title: Courts and commercial powers
chapters66.note: French court culture, Dutch commerce and English political change coexist in a contested European balance.

chapters66.title: Enlightenment and global rivalry
chapters66.note: Britain and France compete overseas; Austria, Prussia and Russia are important continental powers.

chapters66.title: Revolution and Napoleon
chapters66.note: Revolutionary politics and Napoleonic wars transform institutions, borders and artistic subject matter.

chapters66.title: Restoration and new movements
chapters66.note: The Vienna settlement meets liberal and national movements; industry changes society and patronage.

chapters66.title: Revolution and unification
chapters66.note: Revolutions and later state-building reshape Italy and Germany; Realism examines contemporary society.

chapters66.title: Industrial and imperial Europe
chapters66.note: The united German Empire joins the established powers; urban growth and empire frame later nineteenth-century culture.

chapters66.title: Modernity and rival empires
chapters66.note: Industrial change, colonial competition and artistic experiments share this period without a single common cause.

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.title: Impressionism
styles71.note: Light, modern life and independent exhibitions; individual careers extend further.
styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.title: Post-Impressionism

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.title: Neo-Impressionism

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.title: Symbolism

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.title: Arts & Crafts

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

styles71.regionalMethod72: Qualitative study reconstruction. Dates and colour strength are approximate, not measured prevalence; parallel centres do not imply a single origin.

entities.title: Westminster Abbey
entities.creator: Henry of Reyns, John of Gloucester, Robert of Beverley; west towers Nicholas Hawksmoor
entities.note: Henry III commissioned the present Gothic rebuilding.

entities.title: St Paul's Cathedral

photos.caption: Building as photographed; not a reconstruction of this historical phase.

entities.creator: Christopher Wren
entities.note: Rebuilt after the Great Fire of London; the photo's 1657 is not the construction start.

entities.title: Canterbury Cathedral

photos.caption: Building as photographed; not a reconstruction of this historical phase.

entities.built: Founded 597; Norman rebuilding 1070–1077; Gothic choir from 1174
entities.creator: William of Sens and William the Englishman (Gothic choir)
entities.note: Thomas Becket was murdered here in 1170; distinguish the Norman nave history from the Gothic choir.

entities.title: Rouen Cathedral
entities.built: Main rebuilding from the 12th century; later additions through the 19th century
entities.creator: Successive medieval master builders; no single architect
entities.note: Monet painted the façade repeatedly under changing light.

entities.title: Amiens Cathedral
entities.built: 1220 onward; main body largely completed in the 13th century
entities.creator: Robert de Luzarches, Thomas de Cormont, Renaud de Cormont
entities.note: High Gothic cathedral; rib vaults and flying buttresses.

entities.title: Reims Cathedral
entities.built: 1211 onward; major work in the 13th–14th centuries
entities.creator: Jean d'Orbais, Jean-le-Loup, Gaucher de Reims, Bernard de Soissons
entities.note: Traditional coronation site of French kings.

entities.title: Basilica of Saint-Denis
entities.creator: Architect not securely named; Abbot Suger was the patron
entities.note: Suger was the commissioner, not a securely identified architect; an early landmark of Gothic architecture.

entities.title: Chartres Cathedral
entities.built: Main rebuilding c.1194–1220; earlier west front retained
entities.creator: Medieval master builders; individual identity uncertain
entities.note: Stained glass, contrasting spires and the labyrinth.

entities.title: Notre-Dame de Paris

photos.caption: Building as photographed; not a reconstruction of this historical phase.

entities.built: 1163–14th century; restoration in the 19th and 21st centuries
entities.creator: Successive medieval builders; restoration Eugène Viollet-le-Duc and Jean-Baptiste Lassus
entities.note: The medieval cathedral and its later restoration are different construction phases.

entities.title: Sainte-Chapelle
entities.creator: Architect uncertain; commissioned by Louis IX
entities.note: A royal reliquary chapel famous for its extensive stained glass.

entities.title: Notre-Dame du Haut (Ronchamp)

photos.caption: Interior · side chapel

entities.creator: Le Corbusier
entities.note: Sculptural concrete roof and irregular openings; not a Gothic chapel.

entities.title: Cologne Cathedral
entities.creator: Master Gerhard and successive builders; 19th-century completion Ernst Friedrich Zwirner and Richard Voigtel
entities.note: A medieval design completed in the 19th century.

entities.title: Frauenkirche, Dresden
entities.creator: George Bähr; reconstruction team led by Eberhard Burger
entities.note: The Dresden church is Baroque, despite the G annotation in the photo.

entities.title: Karlskirche
entities.creator: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach; completed by Joseph Emanuel Fischer von Erlach
entities.note: Commissioned by Charles VI after a plague epidemic.

entities.title: Sagrada Família
entities.creator: Francisco de Paula del Villar; Antoni Gaudí from 1883; later teams
entities.note: Gaudí transformed the initial neo-Gothic design; no claim of final completion.

entities.title: Barcelona Cathedral
entities.creator: Successive medieval builders; later façade Josep Oriol Mestres and August Font
entities.note: Do not confuse it with Sagrada Família.

entities.title: Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba
entities.creator: Early architect uncertain; Renaissance works Hernán Ruiz I and successors
entities.note: A layered mosque and Christian cathedral; the hypostyle hall and inserted crossing belong to different phases.

entities.title: Turin Cathedral
entities.creator: Meo del Caprina (Amedeo di Francesco)
entities.note: The cathedral body is separate from Guarini's later Chapel of the Holy Shroud.

entities.title: Chapel of the Holy Shroud
entities.creator: Guarino Guarini; earlier project by others
entities.note: An intricate dome adjoining Turin Cathedral; restored after the 1997 fire.

entities.title: Basilica of Superga
entities.creator: Filippo Juvarra
entities.note: Hilltop basilica commissioned by Victor Amadeus II.

entities.title: Sanctuary of Vallinotto
entities.creator: Bernardo Antonio Vittone
entities.note: The photo says Vallinotto, not Vicoforte; patron Antonio Faccio.

entities.title: Santa Maria delle Grazie
entities.creator: Guiniforte Solari (church); tribuna traditionally attributed to Donato Bramante
entities.note: Leonardo's Last Supper is in the convent refectory, not on the church's altar wall.

entities.title: Basilica of Sant'Ambrogio
entities.built: Founded 379–386; present Romanesque fabric mainly 11th–12th centuries
entities.creator: Medieval builders not individually identified; Ambrose was founder; Bramante designed later cloisters
entities.note: Bramante did not design the entire Romanesque basilica.

entities.title: Santa Maria presso San Satiro
aliases: Santa Maria presso San Satiro choir
entities.creator: Donato Bramante (perspective choir and major Renaissance interventions)
entities.note: The shallow illusionistic choir compensates for limited building space.

entities.title: Milan Cathedral

photos.caption: Building as photographed; not a reconstruction of this historical phase.

entities.built: Started 1386; major work continued for centuries
entities.creator: Simone da Orsenigo and successive international builders
entities.note: A collective, long construction history rather than a single architect.

entities.title: Basilica of Sant'Andrea, Mantua

photos.caption: Building as photographed; not a reconstruction of this historical phase.

entities.creator: Leon Battista Alberti (design); Luca Fancelli (execution); Filippo Juvarra (dome)
entities.note: Classical triumphal-arch façade; the dome is later than Alberti's design.

entities.title: San Sebastiano, Mantua
entities.creator: Leon Battista Alberti; execution Luca Fancelli
entities.note: A centrally planned Renaissance church; later alterations complicate the original design.

entities.title: San Giorgio Maggiore
entities.creator: Andrea Palladio; completion Vincenzo Scamozzi
entities.note: Tintoretto's Last Supper is here; classical temple fronts reconcile unequal nave heights.

entities.title: St Mark's Basilica
entities.built: Present church begun 1063; consecrated 1094; later additions
entities.creator: Successive builders; original individual architect uncertain
entities.note: Greek-cross plan, domes and mosaics reflect strong Byzantine connections.

entities.creator: Baldassare Longhena
entities.note: A votive church after the plague; octagonal central plan.

entities.title: Il Redentore

photos.credit:
Il_Redentore.jpg: Wknight94
derivative work: Alberto Fernandez Fernandez (talk)

Il_Redentore.jpg: Wknight94
derivative work: Alberto Fernandez Fernandez (talk)

entities.creator: Andrea Palladio; completion after his death
entities.note: Another plague-votive church; distinguish it from Longhena's Salute.

entities.title: Sant'Apollinare in Classe
entities.creator: Architect unknown; Bishop Ursicinus commissioned it; funded by Julianus Argentarius
entities.note: Located in Classe outside central Ravenna; apse mosaics are a key study feature.

entities.title: Basilica of San Vitale

photos.caption: Building as photographed; not a reconstruction of this historical phase.

entities.creator: Architect unknown; commissioned under Bishop Ecclesius; funded by Julianus Argentarius
entities.note: Octagonal plan and Justinian/Theodora mosaic panels.

entities.title: Florence Cathedral

photos.caption: Building as photographed; not a reconstruction of this historical phase.

entities.creator: Arnolfo di Cambio and successors (church); Filippo Brunelleschi (dome); Emilio De Fabris (façade)
entities.note: The double-shell dome, church body and present façade belong to distinct phases.

entities.title: Basilica of San Lorenzo, Florence

photos.caption: Building as photographed; not a reconstruction of this historical phase.

entities.built: Rebuilding from 1419; completed in later 15th century
entities.creator: Filippo Brunelleschi; later work Antonio Manetti
entities.note: Brunelleschi's church and Old Sacristy differ from Michelangelo's New Sacristy and Laurentian Library.

entities.title: Santo Spirito, Florence
entities.creator: Filippo Brunelleschi; completed by successors
entities.note: Modular proportions and a sequence of semicircular chapels.

entities.title: Santa Maria Novella

photos.caption: Building as photographed; not a reconstruction of this historical phase.

entities.creator: Dominican friars Fra Sisto and Fra Ristoro (church tradition); Leon Battista Alberti (façade)
entities.note: Masaccio's Trinity and Alberti's façade are different works in the same complex.

entities.title: Santa Croce, Florence
entities.creator: Medieval design traditionally attributed to Arnolfo di Cambio; Niccolò Matas (façade)
entities.note: Cimabue's Crucifix belongs to the complex; attribution of the medieval architectural design is not certain.

entities.title: Pazzi Chapel
entities.built: Construction from 1440s; completed after Brunelleschi's death
entities.creator: Traditionally attributed to Filippo Brunelleschi; extent of authorship debated
entities.note: Located in the Santa Croce complex; do not treat debated authorship as fully documented.

entities.title: Brancacci Chapel

photos.caption: Chapel fresco

entities.built: Chapel built before 1386; frescoes c.1423–1420s, completed c.1485
entities.creator: Architect not securely identified; painters Masolino, Masaccio and Filippino Lippi
entities.note: In Santa Maria del Carmine; the artists painted the cycle rather than designing the entire church.

entities.title: Santa Maria delle Carceri
entities.creator: Giuliano da Sangallo
entities.note: Greek-cross central plan; commissioned with support from Lorenzo de' Medici.

entities.title: Siena Cathedral
entities.creator: Successive builders; Giovanni Pisano (part of façade)
entities.note: Striped marble and the unfinished expansion distinguish the complex.

entities.title: Pisa Cathedral
entities.built: Started 1063–1064 (sources differ); consecrated 1118; façade extension 12th century
entities.creator: Buscheto; Rainaldo (extension and façade)
entities.note: Pisan Romanesque; the cathedral, baptistery and leaning campanile are distinct buildings.

entities.title: Scrovegni Chapel

photos.caption: work

entities.creator: Architect not securely documented; Giotto (frescoes); Enrico Scrovegni (patron)
entities.note: Giotto painted the cycle; do not automatically identify him as the architect.

entities.title: Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi
aliases: Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi
entities.creator: Architectural authorship uncertain; Brother Elias supervised construction
entities.note: Lower and upper churches differ; the upper St Francis fresco cycle is traditionally associated with Giotto and his workshop, with scholarly debate.
entities.resolvedTitle102: Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi

entities.title: Tempio Malatestiano
entities.built: Renaissance remodelling from c.1450; left incomplete
entities.creator: Leon Battista Alberti (exterior design); Matteo de' Pasti (execution)
entities.note: Remodelled the existing church of San Francesco for Sigismondo Pandolfo Malatesta.

entities.title: Monreale Cathedral
entities.built: Begun 1170s; main construction in late 12th century
entities.creator: Architect unknown; commissioned by William II of Sicily
entities.note: Norman royal patronage with Byzantine mosaics and Islamic influences.

entities.title: St Peter's Basilica

photos.caption: Building as photographed; not a reconstruction of this historical phase.

entities.creator: Bramante, Raphael, Antonio da Sangallo the Younger, Michelangelo; Carlo Maderno; Gian Lorenzo Bernini (piazza)
entities.note: Michelangelo's dome project, Maderno's nave/façade and Bernini's piazza are distinct contributions.

entities.title: Pantheon, Rome
entities.built: Present building c.118–125 CE; converted to church 609
entities.creator: Architect not securely known; Emperor Hadrian was patron of rebuilding
entities.note: Soufflot designed the Paris Panthéon, not the Roman Pantheon; this is Santa Maria ad Martyres.

entities.title: San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane
aliases: San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane: church

photos.caption: Building as photographed; not a reconstruction of this historical phase.

entities.creator: Francesco Borromini; façade completed by his nephew Bernardo
entities.note: An oval-derived plan and undulating façade; distinguish it from Bernini's Sant'Andrea.

entities.title: Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza
entities.creator: Francesco Borromini
entities.note: Geometric plan and spiral lantern in the former university courtyard.

entities.title: Sant'Andrea al Quirinale
entities.creator: Gian Lorenzo Bernini, with Giovanni de Rossi
entities.note: A transverse oval church, distinct from Borromini's San Carlo nearby.

entities.title: Tempietto, San Pietro in Montorio
aliases: Tempietto at San Pietro in Montorio
entities.creator: Donato Bramante
entities.note: A small commemorative chapel in the courtyard; its precise building date is debated.

entities.title: Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls
aliases: Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls
entities.built: 4th-century basilica; rebuilt after the 1823 fire; reconsecrated 1854
entities.creator: Ancient builders uncertain; rebuilding Pasquale Belli and Luigi Poletti

entities.title: Linear perspective: horizon and vanishing point
aliases: Linear perspective: horizon and vanishing point
entities.note: Orthogonals converge towards a vanishing point on the horizon in single-point perspective. The horizon corresponds to eye level, not necessarily a visible skyline.

entities.title: Atmospheric perspective
entities.note: Distant forms can appear less distinct, lower in contrast and cooler in colour. This differs from the geometric convergence of linear perspective.

entities.title: Centralised plan and Renaissance ideals
entities.note: Circular, square and Greek-cross plans can express geometrical order. A Greek cross has arms of approximately equal length, unlike a longitudinal Latin cross.

entities.title: Disegno and colore

entities.title: Fresco, tempera and oil: identifying technique
aliases: Fresco, tempera and oil: identifying technique
entities.note: Buon fresco uses pigment on fresh plaster; tempera uses an emulsion binder; oil paint dries through oxidation. Support, binder and application are separate questions.

entities.title: Patronage, guilds and artistic commissions
entities.note: Churches, civic bodies, rulers, guilds and private patrons commissioned different subjects and formats. A work's purpose can explain its scale, placement and iconography.

entities.title: Renaissance architectural proportion
entities.note: Architects reinterpreted classical orders, symmetry and measured relationships. Classical appearance can coexist with new construction solutions and Christian functions.

entities.title: Sfumato and chiaroscuro
entities.note: Sfumato softens boundaries through subtle tonal transitions. Chiaroscuro models form through light and shade. The two terms are related but not interchangeable.

entities.title: Assassination of Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo
aliases: Assassination of Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo
entities.note: The assassination on 28 June triggered the July Crisis; it was not the sole underlying cause of the war.

entities.title: Battle of Tannenberg
entities.note: A German victory over Russian forces on the Eastern Front.

entities.title: First Battle of the Marne
entities.note: Stopped the German advance towards Paris; followed by prolonged trench warfare.

entities.title: Mystery and Melancholy of a Street
aliases: Mystery and Melancholy of a Street

photos.license: Copyrighted artwork; reproduction from Wikipedia. Commercial-use permission not established.
photos.caption: Identified work. Sculpture photographs may show later casts or surviving copies.

entities.note: Arcades, shadows and an isolated figure produce the enigmatic atmosphere of Metaphysical painting.
entities.creator: Giorgio de Chirico

entities.title: Panama Canal opens
entities.note: The canal connected Atlantic and Pacific shipping routes.

entities.title: First World War
entities.note: Industrial warfare, rival alliances and imperial competition transformed Europe; the Western Front armistice was 11 November 1918.

entities.title: Black Square

photos.caption: Identified work. Sculpture photographs may show later casts or surviving copies.

entities.note: A foundational Suprematist work; multiple later versions exist.
entities.creator: Kazimir Malevich

entities.title: Treaty of London
entities.note: Secret Allied promises preceded Italy's entry into the war against Austria-Hungary.

entities.title: Hussein–McMahon correspondence
entities.note: Wartime correspondence over Arab independence contained disputed territorial interpretations.

entities.title: Suprematism and Constructivism
entities.note: Suprematism emphasises autonomous geometric form; Constructivist practices often connect materials, construction and social production. The movements overlap historically but are not identical.

entities.title: Dada emerges in Zurich
entities.note: Wartime anti-establishment experimentation; Dada developed differently across cities.
entities.creator: Hugo Ball, Tristan Tzara

entities.title: Sykes–Picot Agreement
entities.note: A secret agreement envisaged spheres of influence in Ottoman Arab territories.

entities.title: Readymade and the artist's act of selection
aliases: Readymade and the artist's act of selection
entities.note: A manufactured object can enter art through selection and presentation. A readymade is not simply a sculpture made from any unusual material.

entities.title: Balfour Declaration
entities.note: British support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine included a clause on the rights of existing non-Jewish communities.

entities.title: Russian February and October Revolutions
entities.note: Tsarist rule fell, followed by Bolshevik seizure of power; calendar conventions explain the month names.

entities.title: United States enters World War I
aliases: United States enters World War I
entities.note: US entry in April altered Allied resources and the diplomatic balance.

entities.title: De Stijl and Neo-Plasticism
entities.note: Restricted colour, orthogonal relationships and compositional balance link painting, furniture and architecture. Mondrian's painting and Rietveld's buildings are distinct applications.

entities.title: Armistice of 11 November
entities.note: Ended fighting between Germany and the Allies; the peace treaty followed in 1919.

entities.title: White on White

photos.license: Image © respective rights holders · MoMA collection
photos.caption: Identified work. Sculpture photographs may show later casts or surviving copies. Shown: Suprematist Composition: White on White · 1918

entities.note: Suprematist painting reduces form and colour to subtle relationships.
entities.creator: Kazimir Malevich

entities.title: Wilson's Fourteen Points
entities.note: A programme for peace; the eventual treaties did not adopt all of its principles.

entities.title: D'Annunzio occupies Fiume
entities.note: A nationalist occupation challenged the postwar settlement; distinguish from the 1924 annexation treaty.

entities.title: Paris Peace Conference
entities.note: The conference negotiated several treaties and the League of Nations framework.

entities.title: Treaty of Versailles
entities.note: The German peace settlement imposed territorial, military and financial terms.

entities.title: Weimar Constitution adopted
entities.note: Established Germany's parliamentary republic; later collapse was not inevitable at its founding.

entities.title: Spatial Construction: series

photos.caption: Contextual example: Gabo's Kinetic Construction (Standing Wave), 1919–1920, shown through documentation/reconstruction. The source's generic Spatial Construction title remains unresolved.

entities.note: Constructivist exploration of space; the source does not securely specify one construction.
entities.creator: Naum Gabo

entities.title: Bauhaus school
entities.note: Founded in Weimar, moved to Dessau and then Berlin; closed under Nazi pressure in 1933.
entities.creator: Walter Gropius, Hannes Meyer, Ludwig Mies van der Rohe

entities.title: Bauhaus: workshop, industry and changing directors
aliases: Bauhaus: workshop, industry and changing directors
entities.note: Gropius, Meyer and Mies led different phases. The school changed location and priorities; Bauhaus cannot be reduced to one fixed visual style.

entities.title: Bloody Christmas in Fiume
entities.note: Italian forces ended D'Annunzio's occupation in December.

entities.title: League of Nations begins operating
entities.note: An attempt at collective security after World War I; the United States did not join.

entities.title: Curtain wall versus load-bearing wall
entities.note: A curtain wall encloses a building while the structural frame carries primary loads. A glass facade is not automatically a curtain wall.

entities.title: International Style and modernist diversity
entities.note: The 1932 exhibition and book popularised a formal category. Functionalism, social housing programmes and regional modernisms cannot all be reduced to that category.

entities.title: Italian Rationalism and political context
entities.note: Geometric clarity and modern materials coexisted with Fascist commissions. Formal innovation alone does not identify the politics of a patron or architect.

entities.title: Pilotis, free plan and free facade
aliases: Pilotis, free plan and free facade
entities.note: Le Corbusier's Five Points also include horizontal windows and roof gardens. A frame separates structural support from partitions and the external enclosure.

entities.title: Reinforced concrete and cantilevers
entities.note: Steel reinforcement helps concrete resist tensile forces. A cantilever projects beyond its support; its structural action differs from a simple span supported at both ends.

entities.title: March on Rome
entities.note: Fascist pressure preceded the king's appointment of Mussolini as prime minister; dictatorship consolidated later.

entities.title: Soviet Union founded
entities.note: The USSR was established in December 1922, not in 1917.

entities.title: French and Belgian occupation of the Ruhr
aliases: French and Belgian occupation of the Ruhr
entities.note: A reparations crisis intensified economic and political instability in Germany.

entities.title: Republic of Turkey proclaimed
entities.note: Atatürk's republic followed the collapse of the Ottoman Empire and a war of independence.

entities.title: Roy Lichtenstein
entities.note: American Pop artist drawing on commercial printing and comics.

entities.title: Dawes Plan
entities.note: Restructured German reparations payments and encouraged US loans.

entities.title: Matteotti murdered and Aventine Secession
entities.note: The socialist deputy's murder provoked an opposition withdrawal; the crisis preceded consolidation of Fascist dictatorship.

entities.title: Surrealist Manifesto published
entities.note: An organised movement explored dreams, automatism and the unconscious.
entities.creator: André Breton

entities.title: Treaty of Rome on Fiume
entities.note: Fiume passed to Italy; distinguish this agreement from the European integration treaties of 1957.

entities.title: Surrealist automatism and dream imagery
entities.note: Automatism reduces deliberate control; illusionistic dream imagery is another Surrealist strategy. Dalí's detailed rendering should not stand for every Surrealist method.

entities.title: Locarno Treaties
entities.note: Diplomatic agreements guaranteed Germany's western borders; eastern borders did not receive identical guarantees.

entities.title: Yellow–Red–Blue

photos.caption: Exact title and artist matched to existing catalogue

entities.note: Painted during Kandinsky's Bauhaus period; structured geometry coexists with freer forms.
entities.creator: Wassily Kandinsky

entities.title: Robert Rauschenberg
entities.note: American artist whose Combines connect painting, sculpture and everyday objects.

entities.title: Baird demonstrates television
entities.note: A public demonstration of a working television system; broadcasting developed in later stages.

entities.title: Fleming discovers penicillin's antibacterial effect
entities.note: Clinical production and widespread use required later work by other researchers.

entities.title: Kellogg–Briand Pact
entities.note: Signatories renounced war as national policy; enforcement proved weak.

entities.title: Yves Klein
entities.note: French artist associated with monochromes, performance and Nouveau Réalisme.

entities.title: Andy Warhol
entities.note: American Pop artist investigating celebrity, consumption and serial reproduction.

entities.title: Lateran Pacts
entities.note: Settled the Roman Question and created Vatican City as a sovereign state.

entities.title: The Treachery of Images

entities.creator: René Magritte

entities.title: Wall Street crash
entities.note: The stock-market collapse accompanied the onset of the Great Depression; the depression had broader causes.

entities.title: Great Depression
entities.note: A severe global economic crisis; dates of recovery varied by country.

entities.title: Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow
aliases: Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow

entities.note: A representative Neo-Plasticist composition; the sheet's generic title may refer to another version.
entities.creator: Piet Mondrian

entities.title: London Naval Treaty
entities.note: An interwar agreement limiting certain categories of naval armament.

entities.title: Urban functional zoning and its critics
aliases: Urban functional zoning and its critics
entities.note: Separating housing, work, recreation and circulation was influential in modernist planning. Critics later questioned its treatment of street life and mixed uses.

entities.title: Statute of Westminster
entities.note: Recognised legislative autonomy for specified dominions; implementation differed among them.

entities.note: Precisely painted soft watches unsettle everyday expectations of time and material solidity.

entities.title: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia proclaimed
entities.note: Ibn Saud unified his domains under the new kingdom's name.

entities.title: Germany leaves the League of Nations
aliases: Germany leaves the League of Nations
entities.note: Withdrawal undermined interwar collective-security arrangements.

entities.title: Hitler appointed German chancellor
entities.note: Appointed on 30 January; dismantling democracy followed through repression and legislation.

entities.title: New Deal begins
entities.note: Roosevelt's programmes addressed relief, recovery and reform during the Depression.

entities.title: Reichstag fire and emergency decree
entities.note: The fire was used to justify suspension of civil liberties and repression of opponents.

entities.title: United States recognises the Soviet Union
aliases: United States recognises the Soviet Union
entities.note: Formal diplomatic relations were established under Roosevelt.

entities.title: The Holocaust and Nazi racial persecution
aliases: The Holocaust and Nazi racial persecution
entities.note: The systematic murder of six million Jews occurred within wider Nazi persecution and mass killing. Distinguish ghettos, concentration camps and extermination centres.

entities.title: Dollfuss assassinated in Austrian Nazi coup attempt
aliases: Dollfuss assassinated in Austrian Nazi coup attempt
entities.note: The failed coup preceded later Austrian annexation by Germany in 1938.

entities.title: Hitler combines presidential and chancellor powers
aliases: Hitler combines presidential and chancellor powers
entities.note: After Hindenburg's death, Hitler consolidated personal dictatorship.

entities.title: Rome Protocols
entities.note: Italy, Austria and Hungary concluded political and economic agreements.

entities.title: Italy invades Ethiopia
entities.note: The invasion exposed the weakness of League sanctions and expanded Fascist imperial ambitions.

entities.title: Wagner Act
entities.note: US legislation protected collective bargaining and established a national labour relations framework.

entities.title: Christo
entities.note: Worked with Jeanne-Claude on temporary large-scale environmental projects; credit the partnership.

entities.title: Remilitarisation of the Rhineland
entities.note: German troops entered a demilitarised zone, violating treaty commitments.

entities.title: Rome–Berlin Axis announced
entities.note: A political alignment preceded later military agreements.

entities.title: Fallingwater
entities.note: A Pennsylvania house combining cantilevered concrete terraces with its waterfall setting; guest-house works continued later.
entities.creator: Frank Lloyd Wright

entities.title: Spanish Civil War
entities.note: Republicans and Nationalists fought with foreign involvement; Franco's victory established a dictatorship.

entities.title: Guernica

photos.license: Copyrighted artwork; reproduction from Wikipedia. Commercial-use permission not established.
photos.caption: Reproduction of Picasso's painting, 1937; original in the Museo Reina Sofía, Madrid.

entities.note: Painted after the bombing of Guernica during the Spanish Civil War, for the Spanish Republic's Paris pavilion.
entities.creator: Pablo Picasso

entities.title: Italy joins the Anti-Comintern Pact
entities.note: Italy joined Germany and Japan in an anti-communist pact; distinguish from the 1940 Tripartite Pact.

entities.title: Italy leaves the League of Nations
aliases: Italy leaves the League of Nations
entities.note: The withdrawal followed international conflict over its invasion of Ethiopia.

entities.title: Montserrat

photos.license: Image rights retained by source; commercial reuse not cleared
photos.caption: La Montserrat, 1936–1937; full sculpture, not one of the later head or mask studies.

entities.note: A sculptural response associated with the Spanish Civil War and the 1937 Spanish pavilion.
entities.creator: Julio González

entities.title: The Angel of the Hearth

photos.credit: Max Ernst · © Artists Rights Society (ARS), New York / ADAGP, Paris

entities.note: A monstrous figure evokes destructive political forces before World War II.
entities.creator: Max Ernst

entities.title: Anschluss: annexation of Austria
entities.note: Nazi Germany annexed Austria in March under coercive political and military pressure.

entities.title: Munich Agreement
entities.note: The Sudetenland was ceded without Czechoslovak participation in the agreement.

entities.title: German occupation of Czech lands
entities.note: The occupation destroyed the remaining Czech state's independence after Munich.

entities.title: Germany invades Poland
entities.note: The invasion on 1 September was followed by British and French declarations of war on 3 September.

entities.title: Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact
entities.note: A non-aggression agreement with secret protocols divided spheres of influence in eastern Europe.

entities.title: Second World War
entities.note: European war began with Germany's invasion of Poland; it became a global conflict with distinct theatres and end dates.

entities.title: Churchill becomes prime minister
entities.note: He took office in May as Germany's western offensive began.

entities.title: De Gaulle's Appeal of 18 June
entities.note: The broadcast from London called for continued resistance and became a symbol of Free France.

entities.title: Dunkirk evacuation
entities.note: Allied troops were evacuated; successful evacuation was not a battlefield victory over the German offensive.

entities.title: Fall of France and Vichy regime
aliases: Fall of France and Vichy regime
entities.note: Military defeat and an armistice led to occupation and an authoritarian collaborationist regime.

entities.title: German invasion of Denmark and Norway
aliases: German invasion of Denmark and Norway
entities.note: The April campaign extended the war into northern Europe.

entities.title: Abstract Expressionism emerges
entities.note: A diverse postwar New York movement; action painting and colour-field approaches are distinct tendencies.
entities.creator: Jackson Pollock, Willem de Kooning, Mark Rothko

entities.title: Action painting and colour-field painting
entities.note: Pollock's gestural processes differ from Rothko's broad colour fields. Both sit within a diverse Abstract Expressionist context.

entities.title: Atlantic Charter
entities.note: Roosevelt and Churchill stated wartime and postwar principles before US entry into the war.

entities.title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
entities.note: 7 December in Hawaii, 8 December in Japan; the date difference in the photo reflects time zones.

entities.title: Operation Barbarossa
entities.note: Germany invaded the Soviet Union, breaking the 1939 non-aggression pact.

entities.title: Roosevelt's Four Freedoms speech
entities.note: Outlined freedom of speech, worship, from want and from fear.

entities.title: Battle of Midway
entities.note: A major US naval victory over Japan in the Pacific.

entities.title: Battle of Stalingrad
entities.note: A major turning point on the Eastern Front; German forces surrendered in February 1943.

entities.title: Cairo and Tehran conferences
entities.note: Separate Allied meetings addressed Asian and European war strategy; participants differed.

entities.title: Italian armistice announced
entities.note: Announced on 8 September after signature on 3 September; occupation and civil conflict followed.

entities.title: D-Day: Normandy landings
entities.note: Allied landings on 6 June opened a major western front.

entities.title: Liberation of Paris
entities.note: Paris was liberated in August through resistance action and Allied advance.

entities.title: Liberation of Rome
entities.note: Allied forces entered Rome on 4 June, two days before D-Day.

entities.title: Battle of the Bulge
entities.note: A German winter offensive in the Ardennes failed to reverse the Allied advance.

entities.title: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
aliases: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
entities.note: The US bombed Hiroshima on 6 August and Nagasaki on 9 August; the human consequences were catastrophic.

entities.title: German surrender and VE Day
entities.note: Surrender was signed on 7 May and took effect on 8 May in western Europe; 9 May is commemorated in Russia.

entities.title: Japan surrenders
entities.note: Surrender was announced on 15 August and formally signed on 2 September.

entities.title: Liberation of Auschwitz
entities.note: Soviet forces liberated the Nazi concentration and extermination camp on 27 January.

entities.title: Mussolini killed and Hitler dies
entities.note: Mussolini was executed on 28 April; Hitler died by suicide on 30 April. These are distinct events.

entities.title: Potsdam Conference
entities.note: Allied leaders met in July–August to address postwar Germany and other unresolved issues.

entities.title: United Nations founded
entities.note: The UN Charter entered into force on 24 October; distinguish from the June signing conference.

entities.title: Yalta Conference
entities.note: Allied leaders discussed the postwar settlement and the planned United Nations.

entities.title: Nuremberg trials
entities.note: The main International Military Tribunal tried leading Nazi officials; subsequent trials followed.

entities.title: Postwar reconstruction and collective housing
entities.note: Housing shortages, welfare policies and construction technology shaped postwar projects. The social programme and the architectural form must be examined together.

entities.title: Decolonisation and unequal independence
entities.note: Political independence followed diverse negotiations and wars. Economic dependence and inherited borders often remained, so independence was not one uniform endpoint.

entities.title: Welfare states and the mixed economy
aliases: Welfare states and the mixed economy
entities.note: Public services, social insurance and economic intervention expanded in different national forms. A welfare state is not equivalent to a fully state-owned economy.

entities.title: Cold War: containment and deterrence
entities.note: Containment aimed to limit Soviet expansion; deterrence sought to discourage attack through threatened costs. Proxy wars and diplomacy were also central.

entities.title: First Indochina War begins
entities.note: The conflict between France and the Viet Minh preceded French withdrawal and partition arrangements in 1954.

entities.title: Iron Curtain speech
entities.note: Churchill's speech in Fulton described the division of Europe and called for Anglo-American cooperation.

entities.title: Italian republic referendum
entities.note: Voting on 2–3 June chose a republic; Enrico De Nicola became provisional head of state later that month.

entities.title: Cominform founded
entities.note: A Soviet-led coordination body for communist parties, distinct from the earlier Comintern.

entities.title: Indian independence and Partition
entities.note: British India became India and Pakistan amid mass displacement and violence.

entities.title: Marshall Plan announced
entities.note: A European recovery programme announced in June; implementation began in 1948.

entities.title: Truman Doctrine
entities.note: US aid to Greece and Turkey became a landmark in Cold War containment policy.

entities.title: Brussels Treaty
entities.note: Created the Western Union; the Western European Union followed the modified treaty in 1954.

entities.title: Gandhi assassinated
entities.note: Gandhi was killed in January after Indian independence and Partition.

entities.title: Israel declares independence
entities.note: The declaration on 14 May preceded an expanding Arab–Israeli war; consequences included mass Palestinian displacement.

entities.title: Italian Constitution enters into force
entities.note: Effective 1 January; the republican referendum was in 1946, not 1948.

entities.title: OEEC established
entities.note: Coordinated European recovery cooperation; the OECD succeeded it in 1961.

entities.title: Republic of Korea and North Korea established
aliases: Republic of Korea and North Korea established
entities.note: Two rival states emerged on the divided Korean peninsula.

entities.title: Berlin Blockade and Airlift
entities.note: Soviet blockade of western Berlin prompted an Allied airlift; the blockade ended in May 1949.

entities.title: Federal Republic of Germany established
entities.note: The Basic Law took effect in May; Adenauer became chancellor in September.

entities.title: German Democratic Republic established
entities.note: The East German state was proclaimed in October in the Soviet occupation zone.

entities.title: NATO founded
entities.note: The North Atlantic Treaty was signed on 4 April; West Germany joined only in 1955.

entities.title: People's Republic of China proclaimed
entities.note: Mao proclaimed the PRC on 1 October following communist victory on the mainland.

entities.title: NATO, Warsaw Pact and non-alignment
entities.note: The two military alliances structured much of Europe, but not every state belonged to either bloc. Non-alignment did not mean an absence of international interests.

entities.title: India becomes a republic
entities.note: Its constitution came into effect on 26 January.

entities.title: Schuman Declaration
entities.note: Proposed pooling coal and steel production; a major step towards European integration.

entities.title: Korean War
entities.note: War began in June 1950; an armistice, not a peace treaty, ended major fighting in July 1953.

entities.title: Notre-Dame du Haut, Ronchamp
entities.note: Sculptural concrete forms distinguish this chapel from the geometric white villas of the 1920s.
entities.creator: Le Corbusier

entities.title: Pop Art emerges
entities.note: British and American strands use mass media and consumer imagery in different ways.
entities.creator: Richard Hamilton, Andy Warhol, Roy Lichtenstein

entities.title: Brutalism, exposed materials and social programmes
aliases: Brutalism, exposed materials and social programmes
entities.note: Brutalism is associated with exposed construction and forceful form, often in public buildings. Not every concrete building is Brutalist, and the label has several origins.

entities.title: Pop Art, reproduction and consumer imagery
aliases: Pop Art, reproduction and consumer imagery
entities.note: Commercial imagery, celebrity and repetition question distinctions between fine art and mass culture. Pop can be critical, ambiguous or fascinated rather than uniformly celebratory.

entities.title: European integration: ECSC, EEC and EU
aliases: European integration: ECSC, EEC and EU
entities.note: Coal and steel cooperation preceded the EEC; Maastricht established the EU later. Signature and entry into force are different dates; the Council of Europe is a separate organisation.

entities.title: Treaty of Paris establishes ECSC
entities.note: Signed in 1951 and effective in 1952; the Coal and Steel Community united six founding states.

entities.title: Unité d'Habitation in Marseille completed
entities.note: A postwar collective housing prototype combining apartments with shared services.
entities.creator: Le Corbusier

entities.title: Stalin dies
entities.note: His death opened a struggle for succession and later changes in Soviet policy.

entities.title: Geneva agreements on Indochina
entities.note: The settlement ended the First Indochina War and temporarily divided Vietnam.

entities.title: Paris Agreements
entities.note: Prepared West German sovereignty and NATO membership and established the Western European Union framework.

entities.title: Warsaw Pact formed
entities.note: Formed after West Germany joined NATO; the two alliances structured much of Cold War Europe.

entities.title: Hungarian uprising
entities.note: A revolt against Soviet-backed rule was suppressed by Soviet military intervention.

entities.title: Khrushchev's Secret Speech
entities.note: Denounced aspects of Stalin's rule; de-Stalinisation had uneven limits.

entities.title: Suez Crisis
entities.note: Britain, France and Israel attacked Egypt after canal nationalisation; international pressure forced withdrawal.

entities.title: International Atomic Energy Agency established
entities.note: An international body for cooperation and safeguards in the peaceful use of nuclear technology.

entities.title: Treaties of Rome signed
entities.note: Signed on 25 March; the EEC and Euratom treaties entered into force on 1 January 1958.

entities.title: Cuban Revolution
entities.note: Castro's movement overthrew Batista; Cold War alignment developed in the following years.

entities.title: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum opens

photos.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA

entities.note: The New York museum's spiral ramp organises a continuous exhibition route.
entities.creator: Frank Lloyd Wright

entities.title: Blue monochromes: series

photos.license: Image © respective rights holders · MoMA collection
photos.caption: Representative work from the series/cycle; the timeline range covers the series, not only this image. Shown: Blue Monochrome · 1961

entities.note: Klein made multiple blue monochromes; the sheet does not identify a specific work or inventory number.
entities.creator: Yves Klein

entities.title: OPEC founded
entities.note: Oil-producing states founded the organisation in Baghdad in September.

entities.title: Year of Africa
entities.note: Seventeen African countries gained independence, within a longer and uneven decolonisation process.

entities.title: Conceptual art
entities.note: The idea, proposition or instruction can take priority over a unique crafted object.
entities.creator: Joseph Kosuth, Sol LeWitt

entities.title: Land art
entities.note: Works engage sites and landscapes; not every work shares the same environmental ethics.
entities.creator: Robert Smithson

entities.title: Minimalism
entities.note: Industrial materials, repetition and the viewer's bodily relation to space challenge traditional composition.
entities.creator: Donald Judd, Carl Andre

entities.title: Minimalism: serial form and the viewer's body
aliases: Minimalism: serial form and the viewer's body
entities.note: Repeated industrial forms and real spatial relationships shift attention from expressive brushwork to the viewer's encounter with objects.

entities.title: Civil rights, feminism and social movements
aliases: Civil rights, feminism and social movements
entities.note: Movements challenged legal and social inequalities through different goals and strategies. Compare voting rights, workplace rights and broader forms of social power.

entities.title: Conceptual art, instructions and documentation
entities.note: The proposition or process may be central while objects, photographs or text document it. Conceptual art does not mean that material presentation is always irrelevant.

entities.title: Land art and site specificity
entities.note: A work's location and physical conditions can be constitutive of it. Moving documentation into a museum is not equivalent to relocating the original site.

entities.title: Performance, body art and temporary work
aliases: Performance, body art and temporary work
entities.note: An action, duration or bodily presence can form the work. Surviving photographs or videos may be documentation rather than the original event itself.

entities.note: East German authorities began closing the border on 13 August.

entities.title: Gagarin's first human spaceflight

entities.note: The US president was killed in Dallas on 22 November.

entities.title: Arte Povera named
entities.note: An Italian critical grouping using humble materials and questioning cultural institutions.
entities.creator: Germano Celant

entities.title: European Communities Merger Treaty takes effect
aliases: European Communities Merger Treaty takes effect
entities.note: A single Commission and Council served the Communities; the separate treaties did not simply disappear.

entities.title: Arte Povera and unconventional materials
entities.note: Artists used materials such as earth, cloth, wood and industrial components to question established artistic and economic values. Povera does not describe a lack of artistic skill.

entities.title: Martin Luther King Jr. and Robert Kennedy assassinated
aliases: Martin Luther King Jr. and Robert Kennedy assassinated
entities.note: King was killed in April and Kennedy in June; distinguish their roles and circumstances.

entities.title: Prague Spring and Warsaw Pact invasion
aliases: Prague Spring and Warsaw Pact invasion
entities.note: Czechoslovak reform efforts were suppressed by an invasion in August.

entities.title: Apollo 11 Moon landing
entities.note: Armstrong and Aldrin landed on the Moon; Collins remained in lunar orbit.

entities.title: Postmodern architecture and historical quotation
entities.note: Historical reference, symbolism and critiques of modernist uniformity take multiple forms. Postmodern is not a label for every building constructed after 1970.

entities.title: High-tech architecture and expressed services
entities.note: Structure and building services may be made visually prominent. Exposed ducts alone are insufficient to identify the movement or architect.

entities.title: Sydney Opera House opens

photos.credit: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand

entities.note: Opened after a long construction process; Utzon left the project in 1966.
entities.creator: Jørn Utzon

entities.title: Khmer Rouge rule in Cambodia
entities.note: Pol Pot's regime perpetrated mass killings, forced labour and widespread persecution.

entities.title: Year of three popes
entities.note: Paul VI died, John Paul I had a brief papacy, and John Paul II was elected.

entities.title: Iranian Revolution and Islamic Republic
entities.note: The monarchy fell and an Islamic Republic was established; the revolution brought together competing forces.

entities.title: Transavanguardia named
entities.note: An Italian critical label associated with a return to expressive painting.
entities.creator: Achille Bonito Oliva

entities.title: Deconstructivist architectural form
entities.note: Fragmentation and disrupted geometries challenge expectations of stable composition. The 1988 MoMA exhibition grouped diverse architects, not a single construction system.

entities.title: Chernobyl nuclear disaster
entities.note: A reactor accident on 26 April had widespread environmental and political consequences.

entities.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
entities.note: Border crossings opened on 9 November; German reunification followed in 1990.

entities.title: Malta Summit
entities.note: Bush and Gorbachev met during the rapid transformation of Cold War Europe.

entities.title: Tiananmen Square crackdown
entities.note: Chinese authorities violently suppressed a protest movement in June.

entities.title: Globalisation and economic interdependence
entities.note: Cross-border trade, finance, production and information increased interdependence. These processes predate 1989 and do not erase national institutions or inequalities.

entities.title: German reunification
entities.note: The German Democratic Republic joined the Federal Republic on 3 October.

entities.title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
entities.note: The USSR ceased to exist in December; successor states followed different political paths.

entities.title: Maastricht Treaty signed
entities.note: Signed on 7 February; the European Union formally began when the treaty entered into force in 1993.

entities.title: European Union established
entities.note: The Maastricht Treaty entered into force on 1 November.

entities.title: NAFTA enters into force
entities.note: A trade agreement between Canada, Mexico and the United States; later replaced by USMCA.

entities.title: September 11 attacks
entities.note: Al-Qaeda attacks in the United States reshaped international security policy.

entities.title: Lehman Brothers bankruptcy
entities.note: The September collapse intensified the global financial crisis; the crisis had begun earlier.

entities.title: Arab Spring uprisings begin
entities.note: Beginning in Tunisia in late 2010, protests spread in 2011 with different outcomes by country.
