entities.title: Angkor
entities.note: Angkor combines temples, reservoirs and urban infrastructure. Angkor Wat and the Bayon belong to different building campaigns; the long range describes the city, not one temple.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Taj Mahal
entities.note: Shah Jahan commissioned this mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal. Read the white marble tomb together with its garden and symmetrical complex; it is a funerary monument, not a royal residence.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Borobudur
entities.note: A Buddhist monument with square terraces below circular platforms and a crowning stupa. The ascending route organizes reliefs and repeated stupas into a spatial sequence.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Petra
entities.note: Nabataean Petra combined caravan commerce, rock-cut architecture and careful water management. Carved facades do not mean that every part of the city was cut into rock.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Machu Picchu
entities.note: The Inca site joins stone buildings, terraces and steep mountain terrain. Its fifteenth-century setting distinguishes it from earlier Andean cultures such as the Moche.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Chichén Itzá
entities.note: Temple pyramids, a large ball court and other monuments show a Maya city with wider Mesoamerican connections. Do not confuse it with Teotihuacan in central Mexico.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Teotihuacan
entities.note: The Avenue of the Dead links monumental precincts including the Sun and Moon pyramids. The city flourished many centuries before the Aztec Empire; its builders should not be labelled Aztec.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Rapa Nui: moai
entities.note: The moai are monumental stone figures associated with a Polynesian island society. Many stand on ceremonial platforms called ahu. The range is a broad period, not a date for every statue.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Himeji Castle
entities.note: White plastered surfaces cover a sophisticated timber castle. Gates, walls and routes form a defensive system: its appearance is not simply ornamental.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Forbidden City
entities.note: Beijing's imperial palace developed as a hierarchy of courts and halls along an axis. The initial Ming construction dates do not imply that every surviving structure is original.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Temple of Heaven
entities.note: This ceremonial complex relates imperial ritual to ideas of heaven and earth. Read its symbolism and layout as a religious-political landscape rather than a residential palace.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Potala Palace
entities.note: The palace was a winter residence of the Dalai Lama and a centre of Tibetan Buddhist authority. Its major seventeenth-century development stands on a site with earlier history.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Lalibela: rock-hewn churches
entities.note: Eleven medieval churches were carved from rock and connected by trenches and passages. Excavating spaces and leaving structural masses produces architecture by subtraction.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Great Zimbabwe
entities.note: The ruins record a Shona urban and trading centre. Carefully fitted granite walls, especially the Great Enclosure, challenge the idea that monumental African architecture was limited to Egypt.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Djenné: historic town
entities.note: Earthen construction links the town's buildings to local materials and continuing maintenance. The range describes a historic urban phase, not the construction date of today's Great Mosque.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Persepolis
entities.note: Darius I began the Achaemenid palace complex on a monumental terrace. Reliefs and ceremonial spaces expressed imperial authority; this is not a Greek polis.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Sanchi
entities.note: Stupas, gateways and other remains trace a long Buddhist history beginning in the Mauryan period. The stupa is a sacred mound or reliquary monument, not an ordinary dwelling.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Khajuraho
entities.note: The surviving temples combine towered sanctuaries with extensive sculpture. Both Hindu and Jain monuments are represented; reducing the site to erotic imagery misses its wider religious programme.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Bagan
entities.note: Thousands of Buddhist monuments form a landscape shaped by patronage and merit-making. The selected range describes the principal building era, not every restoration.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Samarkand
entities.note: Samarkand links Silk Road exchange with Timurid monuments and scholarship. The Registan, Bibi-Khanum Mosque and Ulugh Beg's observatory have different functions and building histories.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Hampi
entities.note: The former Vijayanagara capital brings together temples, royal structures and a dramatic rocky landscape. The ruins belong to a major southern Indian kingdom, not to Mughal Agra.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Konark Sun Temple
entities.note: The temple gives architectural form to the chariot of Surya, the sun god. Carved wheels and horses turn an entire building into a religious image.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Mogao Caves
entities.note: Wall paintings and sculpture preserve many centuries of Buddhist art along the Silk Road. The caves also connect art history with manuscripts and intercultural exchange.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

entities.title: Longmen Grottoes
entities.style: Northern Wei and Tang Buddhist sculpture
entities.note: Rock-cut Buddhist images reveal changing styles and patronage, especially under Northern Wei and Tang rule. Compare carved stone at Longmen with painted cave interiors at Mogao.
entities.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance
styles103: Northern Wei and Tang Buddhist sculpture

places.title: Westminster Abbey
places.creator: Henry of Reyns, John of Gloucester, Robert of Beverley; west towers Nicholas Hawksmoor
places.note: Henry III commissioned the present Gothic rebuilding.

places.title: St Paul's Cathedral
places.creator: Christopher Wren
places.note: Rebuilt after the Great Fire of London; the photo's 1657 is not the construction start.

places.title: Canterbury Cathedral
places.built: Founded 597; Norman rebuilding 1070–1077; Gothic choir from 1174
places.creator: William of Sens and William the Englishman (Gothic choir)
places.note: Thomas Becket was murdered here in 1170; distinguish the Norman nave history from the Gothic choir.

places.title: Rouen Cathedral
places.built: Main rebuilding from the 12th century; later additions through the 19th century
places.creator: Successive medieval master builders; no single architect
places.note: Monet painted the façade repeatedly under changing light.

places.title: Amiens Cathedral
places.built: 1220 onward; main body largely completed in the 13th century
places.creator: Robert de Luzarches, Thomas de Cormont, Renaud de Cormont
places.note: High Gothic cathedral; rib vaults and flying buttresses.

places.title: Reims Cathedral
places.built: 1211 onward; major work in the 13th–14th centuries
places.creator: Jean d'Orbais, Jean-le-Loup, Gaucher de Reims, Bernard de Soissons
places.note: Traditional coronation site of French kings.

places.title: Basilica of Saint-Denis
places.creator: Architect not securely named; Abbot Suger was the patron
places.note: Suger was the commissioner, not a securely identified architect; an early landmark of Gothic architecture.

places.title: Chartres Cathedral
places.built: Main rebuilding c.1194–1220; earlier west front retained
places.creator: Medieval master builders; individual identity uncertain
places.note: Stained glass, contrasting spires and the labyrinth.

places.title: Notre-Dame de Paris
places.built: 1163–14th century; restoration in the 19th and 21st centuries
places.creator: Successive medieval builders; restoration Eugène Viollet-le-Duc and Jean-Baptiste Lassus
places.note: The medieval cathedral and its later restoration are different construction phases.

places.title: Sainte-Chapelle
places.creator: Architect uncertain; commissioned by Louis IX
places.note: A royal reliquary chapel famous for its extensive stained glass.

places.title: Notre-Dame du Haut (Ronchamp)
places.creator: Le Corbusier
places.note: Sculptural concrete roof and irregular openings; not a Gothic chapel.

places.title: Cologne Cathedral
places.creator: Master Gerhard and successive builders; 19th-century completion Ernst Friedrich Zwirner and Richard Voigtel
places.note: A medieval design completed in the 19th century.

places.title: Frauenkirche, Dresden
places.creator: George Bähr; reconstruction team led by Eberhard Burger
places.note: The Dresden church is Baroque, despite the G annotation in the photo.

places.title: Karlskirche
places.creator: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach; completed by Joseph Emanuel Fischer von Erlach
places.note: Commissioned by Charles VI after a plague epidemic.

places.title: Sagrada Família
places.creator: Francisco de Paula del Villar; Antoni Gaudí from 1883; later teams
places.note: Gaudí transformed the initial neo-Gothic design; no claim of final completion.

places.title: Barcelona Cathedral
places.creator: Successive medieval builders; later façade Josep Oriol Mestres and August Font
places.note: Do not confuse it with Sagrada Família.

places.title: Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba
places.creator: Early architect uncertain; Renaissance works Hernán Ruiz I and successors
places.note: A layered mosque and Christian cathedral; the hypostyle hall and inserted crossing belong to different phases.

places.title: Turin Cathedral
places.creator: Meo del Caprina (Amedeo di Francesco)
places.note: The cathedral body is separate from Guarini's later Chapel of the Holy Shroud.

places.title: Chapel of the Holy Shroud
places.creator: Guarino Guarini; earlier project by others
places.note: An intricate dome adjoining Turin Cathedral; restored after the 1997 fire.

places.title: Basilica of Superga
places.creator: Filippo Juvarra
places.note: Hilltop basilica commissioned by Victor Amadeus II.

places.title: Sanctuary of Vallinotto
places.creator: Bernardo Antonio Vittone
places.note: The photo says Vallinotto, not Vicoforte; patron Antonio Faccio.

places.title: Santa Maria delle Grazie
places.creator: Guiniforte Solari (church); tribuna traditionally attributed to Donato Bramante
places.note: Leonardo's Last Supper is in the convent refectory, not on the church's altar wall.

places.title: Basilica of Sant'Ambrogio
places.built: Founded 379–386; present Romanesque fabric mainly 11th–12th centuries
places.creator: Medieval builders not individually identified; Ambrose was founder; Bramante designed later cloisters
places.note: Bramante did not design the entire Romanesque basilica.

places.title: Santa Maria presso San Satiro
places.creator: Donato Bramante (perspective choir and major Renaissance interventions)
places.note: The shallow illusionistic choir compensates for limited building space.

places.title: Milan Cathedral
places.built: Started 1386; major work continued for centuries
places.creator: Simone da Orsenigo and successive international builders
places.note: A collective, long construction history rather than a single architect.

places.title: Basilica of Sant'Andrea, Mantua
places.creator: Leon Battista Alberti (design); Luca Fancelli (execution); Filippo Juvarra (dome)
places.note: Classical triumphal-arch façade; the dome is later than Alberti's design.

places.title: San Sebastiano, Mantua
places.creator: Leon Battista Alberti; execution Luca Fancelli
places.note: A centrally planned Renaissance church; later alterations complicate the original design.

places.title: San Giorgio Maggiore
places.creator: Andrea Palladio; completion Vincenzo Scamozzi
places.note: Tintoretto's Last Supper is here; classical temple fronts reconcile unequal nave heights.

places.title: St Mark's Basilica
places.built: Present church begun 1063; consecrated 1094; later additions
places.creator: Successive builders; original individual architect uncertain
places.note: Greek-cross plan, domes and mosaics reflect strong Byzantine connections.

places.title: Santa Maria della Salute
places.creator: Baldassare Longhena
places.note: A votive church after the plague; octagonal central plan.

places.title: Sant'Apollinare in Classe
places.creator: Architect unknown; Bishop Ursicinus commissioned it; funded by Julianus Argentarius
places.note: Located in Classe outside central Ravenna; apse mosaics are a key study feature.

places.title: Basilica of San Vitale
places.creator: Architect unknown; commissioned under Bishop Ecclesius; funded by Julianus Argentarius
places.note: Octagonal plan and Justinian/Theodora mosaic panels.

places.title: Florence Cathedral
places.creator: Arnolfo di Cambio and successors (church); Filippo Brunelleschi (dome); Emilio De Fabris (façade)
places.note: The double-shell dome, church body and present façade belong to distinct phases.

places.title: Basilica of San Lorenzo, Florence
places.built: Rebuilding from 1419; completed in later 15th century
places.creator: Filippo Brunelleschi; later work Antonio Manetti
places.note: Brunelleschi's church and Old Sacristy differ from Michelangelo's New Sacristy and Laurentian Library.

places.title: Santo Spirito, Florence
places.creator: Filippo Brunelleschi; completed by successors
places.note: Modular proportions and a sequence of semicircular chapels.

places.title: Santa Maria Novella
places.creator: Dominican friars Fra Sisto and Fra Ristoro (church tradition); Leon Battista Alberti (façade)
places.note: Masaccio's Trinity and Alberti's façade are different works in the same complex.

places.title: Santa Croce, Florence
places.creator: Medieval design traditionally attributed to Arnolfo di Cambio; Niccolò Matas (façade)
places.note: Cimabue's Crucifix belongs to the complex; attribution of the medieval architectural design is not certain.

places.title: Pazzi Chapel
places.built: Construction from 1440s; completed after Brunelleschi's death
places.creator: Traditionally attributed to Filippo Brunelleschi; extent of authorship debated
places.note: Located in the Santa Croce complex; do not treat debated authorship as fully documented.

places.title: Brancacci Chapel
places.built: Chapel built before 1386; frescoes c.1423–1420s, completed c.1485
places.creator: Architect not securely identified; painters Masolino, Masaccio and Filippino Lippi
places.note: In Santa Maria del Carmine; the artists painted the cycle rather than designing the entire church.

places.title: Santa Maria delle Carceri
places.creator: Giuliano da Sangallo
places.note: Greek-cross central plan; commissioned with support from Lorenzo de' Medici.

places.title: Siena Cathedral
places.creator: Successive builders; Giovanni Pisano (part of façade)
places.note: Striped marble and the unfinished expansion distinguish the complex.

places.title: Pisa Cathedral
places.built: Started 1063–1064 (sources differ); consecrated 1118; façade extension 12th century
places.creator: Buscheto; Rainaldo (extension and façade)
places.note: Pisan Romanesque; the cathedral, baptistery and leaning campanile are distinct buildings.

places.title: Scrovegni Chapel
places.creator: Architect not securely documented; Giotto (frescoes); Enrico Scrovegni (patron)
places.note: Giotto painted the cycle; do not automatically identify him as the architect.

places.title: Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi
places.creator: Architectural authorship uncertain; Brother Elias supervised construction
places.note: Lower and upper churches differ; the upper St Francis fresco cycle is traditionally associated with Giotto and his workshop, with scholarly debate.

places.title: Tempio Malatestiano
places.built: Renaissance remodelling from c.1450; left incomplete
places.creator: Leon Battista Alberti (exterior design); Matteo de' Pasti (execution)
places.note: Remodelled the existing church of San Francesco for Sigismondo Pandolfo Malatesta.

places.title: Monreale Cathedral
places.built: Begun 1170s; main construction in late 12th century
places.creator: Architect unknown; commissioned by William II of Sicily
places.note: Norman royal patronage with Byzantine mosaics and Islamic influences.

places.title: St Peter's Basilica
places.creator: Bramante, Raphael, Antonio da Sangallo the Younger, Michelangelo; Carlo Maderno; Gian Lorenzo Bernini (piazza)
places.note: Michelangelo's dome project, Maderno's nave/façade and Bernini's piazza are distinct contributions.

places.title: Pantheon, Rome
places.built: Present building c.118–125 CE; converted to church 609
places.creator: Architect not securely known; Emperor Hadrian was patron of rebuilding
places.note: Soufflot designed the Paris Panthéon, not the Roman Pantheon; this is Santa Maria ad Martyres.

places.title: San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane
places.creator: Francesco Borromini; façade completed by his nephew Bernardo
places.note: An oval-derived plan and undulating façade; distinguish it from Bernini's Sant'Andrea.

places.title: Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza
places.creator: Francesco Borromini
places.note: Geometric plan and spiral lantern in the former university courtyard.

places.title: Sant'Andrea al Quirinale
places.creator: Gian Lorenzo Bernini, with Giovanni de Rossi
places.note: A transverse oval church, distinct from Borromini's San Carlo nearby.

places.title: Tempietto, San Pietro in Montorio
places.creator: Donato Bramante
places.note: A small commemorative chapel in the courtyard; its precise building date is debated.

places.title: Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls
places.built: 4th-century basilica; rebuilt after the 1823 fire; reconsecrated 1854
places.creator: Ancient builders uncertain; rebuilding Pasquale Belli and Luigi Poletti
places.note: The photo's San Paolo fuori le mura is interpreted as the Roman basilica.

places.title: Sistine Chapel
places.creator: Construction associated with Baccio Pontelli and Giovannino de' Dolci; Michelangelo (painting)
places.note: Michelangelo painted the ceiling and Last Judgement; he was not the chapel's original builder.

places.title: Sant'Agnese in Agone
places.creator: Girolamo and Carlo Rainaldi; Francesco Borromini; later Carlo Rainaldi
places.note: Several architects shaped the church; not a single-author façade-and-dome project.

places.title: Church of the Gesù
places.creator: Giacomo Barozzi da Vignola (plan); Giacomo della Porta (façade and dome)
places.note: Mother church of the Jesuits; later Baroque decoration should be separated from the initial architecture.

places.title: San Luigi dei Francesi
places.creator: Giacomo della Porta and Domenico Fontana (major later construction)
places.note: Caravaggio's three Saint Matthew paintings are in the Contarelli Chapel.

places.title: Santa Maria Maggiore
places.creator: Early architect unknown; Ferdinando Fuga (18th-century façade)
places.note: Early Christian mosaics survive within a building with many later chapels and façades.

places.title: Santa Maria del Popolo
places.creator: Renaissance attribution debated; Bramante (choir); Raphael (Chigi Chapel); Bernini (later works)
places.note: Cerasi Chapel contains Caravaggio's Conversion of Saint Paul and Crucifixion of Saint Peter.

places.title: Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran
places.creator: Francesco Borromini (interior); Alessandro Galilei (façade)
places.note: Rome's cathedral; distinguish Galilei's façade from Borromini's interior.

places.title: Santa Costanza
places.creator: Architect unknown; imperial patronage associated with Constantina
places.note: Originally an imperial mausoleum; central plan with an ambulatory and mosaics.

places.title: Santa Maria della Pace
places.creator: Donato Bramante (cloister); Pietro da Cortona (façade)
places.note: The photo's two names refer to different parts, not competing attributions of the same façade.

places.title: Colosseum
places.note: Flavian amphitheatre; inaugurated by Titus in 80, with later additions.

places.title: Angkor
places.note: Angkor combines temples, reservoirs and urban infrastructure. Angkor Wat and the Bayon belong to different building campaigns; the long range describes the city, not one temple.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance
places.photoScope108: Angkor Wat, one monument within the wider Angkor site

places.title: Taj Mahal
places.note: Shah Jahan commissioned this mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal. Read the white marble tomb together with its garden and symmetrical complex; it is a funerary monument, not a royal residence.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Borobudur
places.note: A Buddhist monument with square terraces below circular platforms and a crowning stupa. The ascending route organizes reliefs and repeated stupas into a spatial sequence.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Petra
places.note: Nabataean Petra combined caravan commerce, rock-cut architecture and careful water management. Carved facades do not mean that every part of the city was cut into rock.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Machu Picchu
places.note: The Inca site joins stone buildings, terraces and steep mountain terrain. Its fifteenth-century setting distinguishes it from earlier Andean cultures such as the Moche.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Chichén Itzá
places.note: Temple pyramids, a large ball court and other monuments show a Maya city with wider Mesoamerican connections. Do not confuse it with Teotihuacan in central Mexico.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Teotihuacan
places.note: The Avenue of the Dead links monumental precincts including the Sun and Moon pyramids. The city flourished many centuries before the Aztec Empire; its builders should not be labelled Aztec.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Rapa Nui: moai
places.note: The moai are monumental stone figures associated with a Polynesian island society. Many stand on ceremonial platforms called ahu. The range is a broad period, not a date for every statue.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Himeji Castle
places.note: White plastered surfaces cover a sophisticated timber castle. Gates, walls and routes form a defensive system: its appearance is not simply ornamental.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Forbidden City
places.note: Beijing's imperial palace developed as a hierarchy of courts and halls along an axis. The initial Ming construction dates do not imply that every surviving structure is original.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Temple of Heaven
places.note: This ceremonial complex relates imperial ritual to ideas of heaven and earth. Read its symbolism and layout as a religious-political landscape rather than a residential palace.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Potala Palace
places.note: The palace was a winter residence of the Dalai Lama and a centre of Tibetan Buddhist authority. Its major seventeenth-century development stands on a site with earlier history.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Lalibela: rock-hewn churches
places.note: Eleven medieval churches were carved from rock and connected by trenches and passages. Excavating spaces and leaving structural masses produces architecture by subtraction.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Great Zimbabwe
places.note: The ruins record a Shona urban and trading centre. Carefully fitted granite walls, especially the Great Enclosure, challenge the idea that monumental African architecture was limited to Egypt.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Djenné: historic town
places.note: Earthen construction links the town's buildings to local materials and continuing maintenance. The range describes a historic urban phase, not the construction date of today's Great Mosque.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance
places.photoScope108: Great Mosque of Djenné, within the historic town; the current mosque is later than the urban phase

places.title: Persepolis
places.note: Darius I began the Achaemenid palace complex on a monumental terrace. Reliefs and ceremonial spaces expressed imperial authority; this is not a Greek polis.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Sanchi
places.note: Stupas, gateways and other remains trace a long Buddhist history beginning in the Mauryan period. The stupa is a sacred mound or reliquary monument, not an ordinary dwelling.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Khajuraho
places.note: The surviving temples combine towered sanctuaries with extensive sculpture. Both Hindu and Jain monuments are represented; reducing the site to erotic imagery misses its wider religious programme.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Bagan
places.note: Thousands of Buddhist monuments form a landscape shaped by patronage and merit-making. The selected range describes the principal building era, not every restoration.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Samarkand
places.note: Samarkand links Silk Road exchange with Timurid monuments and scholarship. The Registan, Bibi-Khanum Mosque and Ulugh Beg's observatory have different functions and building histories.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Hampi
places.note: The former Vijayanagara capital brings together temples, royal structures and a dramatic rocky landscape. The ruins belong to a major southern Indian kingdom, not to Mughal Agra.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Konark Sun Temple
places.note: The temple gives architectural form to the chariot of Surya, the sun god. Carved wheels and horses turn an entire building into a religious image.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Mogao Caves
places.note: Wall paintings and sculpture preserve many centuries of Buddhist art along the Silk Road. The caves also connect art history with manuscripts and intercultural exchange.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance

places.title: Longmen Grottoes
places.style: Northern Wei and Tang Buddhist sculpture
places.note: Rock-cut Buddhist images reveal changing styles and patronage, especially under Northern Wei and Tang rule. Compare carved stone at Longmen with painted cave interiors at Mogao.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative site position, rounded; not a boundary or entrance
styles103: Northern Wei and Tang Buddhist sculpture

places.title: Stonehenge
places.note: Megalithic construction combines upright stones and lintels. Study the monument as a sequence of prehistoric phases rather than a building made at one moment.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Skara Brae
places.note: Stone-built houses preserve domestic space and fittings. Compare this settlement with ceremonial stone circles: prehistoric architecture also includes everyday dwellings.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Newgrange
places.note: A passage leads into a chamber within a mound. Its carved stones and relationship to the winter solstice connect burial architecture, imagery and the seasonal cycle.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Mycenae
places.note: Fortification walls, the Lion Gate and tholos tombs belong to Bronze Age Greece. They precede the Classical temples of fifth-century BCE Athens.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Delphi
places.note: The sanctuary of Apollo linked an oracle, treasuries, temples and athletic competition. Its hillside setting differs from a regular urban grid.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Olympia
places.note: A sanctuary of Zeus and the setting of the ancient Olympic Games. Religious monuments and athletic spaces belong to the same complex.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Ephesus
places.note: The Library of Celsus and theatre exemplify monumental urban life. Distinguish the Roman city remains from the earlier fame of the Temple of Artemis.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Carthage
places.note: A Phoenician foundation became Rome's great Mediterranean rival. The archaeological site also contains a later Roman city; its remains do not all belong to one culture.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Leptis Magna
places.note: Public buildings, streets and harbour remains reveal a major Roman city in North Africa. Compare provincial Roman urbanism with monuments in Rome itself.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Timgad
places.note: Trajan founded the colony in 100 CE. The orthogonal street network makes it useful for learning cardo, decumanus and Roman planning beyond Italy.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Ajanta Caves
places.note: Monastic spaces, worship halls, paintings and sculpture form a Buddhist cave complex. Distinguish this context from Ellora's multiple religious traditions.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Ellora Caves
places.style: Buddhist, Hindu and Jain rock-cut architecture
places.note: Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments coexist at Ellora. The Kailasa temple demonstrates how subtractive carving can produce an apparently freestanding architectural mass.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.
styles103: Buddhist, Hindu and Jain rock-cut architecture

places.title: Elephanta Caves
places.note: The principal cave centres on Shiva and monumental sculptural programmes. It should not be classified as a Buddhist monastery simply because it is rock-cut.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Fatehpur Sikri
places.note: Akbar's planned capital combines courtly and religious spaces. Compare it with the later Taj Mahal: both are Mughal, but one is a city and the other a mausoleum.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Humayun's Tomb
places.note: A monumental tomb set in a formal garden, important for the development of Mughal funerary architecture. Its function and setting provide context for the later Taj Mahal.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Qutb Minar
places.note: The tall minaret belongs to an early Islamic monumental complex in Delhi. Its long construction history predates the Mughal period.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Tōdai-ji
places.note: An eighth-century Buddhist foundation associated with the Great Buddha. Present buildings include later reconstructions, so foundation and surviving fabric have different dates.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Itsukushima Shrine
places.note: The shrine's relationship to tidal water and the sacred island is central to its design. The twelfth-century development should not be confused with the dates of later repairs.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Brasília: civic centre
places.creator: Urban plan: Lúcio Costa; civic buildings: Oscar Niemeyer
places.note: Lúcio Costa's urban plan and Oscar Niemeyer's civic buildings make Brasília a key modernist capital. Urban layout and individual buildings are related but distinct design scales.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Chandigarh Capitol Complex
places.creator: Le Corbusier
places.note: Le Corbusier's governmental complex connects exposed concrete, monumental form and climate-conscious design. It belongs to a planned city developed after Indian independence.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Zollverein: Shaft XII
places.creator: Fritz Schupp and Martin Kremmer
places.note: The coal-mining complex links industrial production with carefully ordered modern architecture. Later reuse makes it useful for comparing original function and heritage adaptation.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Le Havre: reconstructed centre
places.creator: Auguste Perret and team
places.note: Auguste Perret led the postwar rebuilding of the city centre. A consistent structural vocabulary and urban plan show modern reconstruction at the scale of a whole district.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: White City of Tel Aviv
places.note: Modernist buildings adapt European design ideas to local climatic conditions. The district illustrates the international circulation and local transformation of architectural principles.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.

places.title: Fallingwater
places.creator: Frank Lloyd Wright
places.note: Frank Lloyd Wright's house joins cantilevered terraces with a waterfall and rocky site. Learn the relationship between structure, interior space and landscape rather than treating the house as an isolated object.
places.coordinatePrecision106: Representative position of the named site; dates describe the selected historical phase, not every surviving structure.
